questions.q: According to Genesis chapter one, on which day of creation did God make light and separate it from darkness?
o: First day
Fourth day
Second day
Sixth day
questions.e: On the first day, God said 'Let there be light' and separated light from darkness, calling them day and night. This is recorded in Genesis 1:3-5.
questions.p: For first day, God talk say make light dey, e separate am from darkness, e call dem day and night. Dis one dey for Genesis 1:3-5.

questions.q: In the creation account of Genesis chapter one, what name did God give to the dry land that appeared when the waters were gathered together?
o: Heaven
Eden
Garden
Earth
questions.e: God called the dry land 'Earth' and the gathered waters 'Seas', as recorded in Genesis 1:9-10. This happened on the third day of creation.
questions.p: God call the dry ground 'Earth' and the water wey gather together 'Seas', dis dey for Genesis 1:9-10. Na for third day dis one happen.

questions.q: According to Genesis chapter two, what material did God use to form the first man, Adam?
o: Clay from a potter's wheel
Dust of the ground
Water from a river
Rib bone
questions.e: Genesis 2:7 says the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living being.
questions.p: Genesis 2:7 talk say God form man from dust wey dey ground, e blow breath enter im nose, man become living being.

questions.q: In Genesis chapter two, why did God decide to make a woman as a companion for Adam?
o: Because Adam asked for a helper
Because Adam was unable to name the animals alone
Because it was not good for man to be alone
Because the animals rejected Adam
questions.e: God said, 'It is not good that man should be alone; I will make him a helper comparable to him.' This is found in Genesis 2:18, leading to the creation of Eve.
questions.p: God talk say 'e no good make man dey alone; I go make helper wey fit am.' Dis one dey for Genesis 2:18, na im lead to how Eve come dey.

questions.q: According to Genesis chapter two, what responsibility did God give Adam regarding the living creatures in the Garden of Eden?
o: To build shelters for them
To give them names
To sacrifice them to God
To teach them to multiply
questions.e: God brought every beast and bird to Adam to see what he would call them, and whatever Adam called each creature became its name. This is recorded in Genesis 2:19-20.
questions.p: God bring every animal and bird come to Adam make e see wetin e go call dem, and the name wey Adam call am na im remain. Dis dey for Genesis 2:19-20.

questions.q: Reading the creation narrative in Genesis chapter one carefully, which of these shows that God created mainly by the power of His spoken word, demonstrating His sovereignty?
o: God said, 'Let there be...' and it was so
God used materials that already existed in heaven
God consulted with the angels before each creation
God rested before starting each new work
questions.e: Throughout Genesis chapter one, the phrase 'And God said... and it was so' repeats for each act of creation, showing that His word alone had the power to bring things into existence, proving His sovereign authority over all creation.
questions.p: For Genesis chapter one, di phrase 'God talk... e happen so' dey repeat for every creation, e show say na im word get power to bring tin come dey, dis show say God get full control (sovereignty) ova everytin.

questions.q: Based on the correct order of events in Genesis chapter one, which of the following was created before the sun, moon, and stars were made?
o: Cattle and beasts of the earth
Mankind
Fish of the sea
Light
questions.e: Light was created on the first day (Genesis 1:3-5), while the sun, moon, and stars were created later on the fourth day (Genesis 1:14-19). This shows light existed before these heavenly bodies were formed.
questions.p: Light na im God create for first day (Genesis 1:3-5), but sun, moon and stars na for fourth day dem come (Genesis 1:14-19). So light dey before dis heavenly bodies.

questions.q: According to Genesis chapter two, the river that flowed out of Eden divided into four headwaters. Which of these rivers was described as flowing round the whole land of Havilah, a place known for gold?
o: Gihon
Euphrates
Pishon
Tigris
questions.e: Genesis 2:11 specifically names the Pishon as the river that surrounded the whole land of Havilah, where there was gold. The other three rivers mentioned, Gihon, Tigris and Euphrates, are described differently in the passage.
questions.p: Genesis 2:11 talk say na Pishon river dey waka round di whole land of Havilah, where gold dey. Di oda rivers wey dem mention, Gihon, Tigris and Euphrates, get different description for di passage.

questions.q: In the Genesis account, what was the first thing Adam and Eve did to cover their nakedness immediately after they sinned?
o: They wove grass into clothing
They hid under tree bark
They sewed fig leaves together
They wore garments of animal skin
questions.e: As soon as Adam and Eve ate the forbidden fruit, their eyes were opened and they sewed fig leaves together to make coverings for themselves. God later made them coats of skin. See Genesis 3:7.
questions.p: As Adam and Eve chop di forbidden fruit, dem sew fig leaves togeda make dem cover demsef. Na later God yarn make dem wear animal skin. Dis dey for Genesis 3:7.

questions.q: Who became the first murder victim recorded in the Bible, killed by his own brother out of jealousy?
o: Enoch
Cain
Seth
Abel
questions.e: Cain was angry that God accepted Abel's offering but rejected his, so he killed Abel in the field, making Abel the first murder victim in the Bible. See Genesis 4:8.
questions.p: Cain vex because God accept Abel offering but reject im own, so e kill Abel for bush. Na Abel be di first person wey dem kill for Bible. Genesis 4:8 talk am.

questions.q: As part of God's judgement after the fall in the garden of Eden, what did He pronounce concerning the ground because of Adam's sin?
o: It would be cursed to produce thorns and thistles, making man toil for food
It would be flooded immediately
It would never again produce any crop
It would swallow up Adam's descendants
questions.e: God told Adam that because of his disobedience, the ground was cursed and would bring forth thorns and thistles, so he would eat bread only through painful toil. See Genesis 3:17-18.
questions.p: God tell Adam say because im disobey, ground go dey cursed and e go bring thorns and thistles, so Adam go dey sweat before e fit chop. Genesis 3:17-18 talk am.

questions.q: What sign did God give to Noah as a covenant promise that He would never again destroy all living creatures with a flood?
o: An olive branch
A rainbow
A dove
An altar of stones
questions.e: After the flood, God set the rainbow in the clouds as a sign of His everlasting covenant never to destroy the earth with a flood again. See Genesis 9:13.
questions.p: After di flood, God put rainbow for sky as sign say E no go use flood destroy di earth again. Na covenant promise. Genesis 9:13 talk am.

questions.q: According to God's instruction to Noah before the flood, how many of each unclean animal was he commanded to take into the ark?
o: Four pairs
Two (one pair)
Three
Seven pairs
questions.e: God instructed Noah to take seven pairs of every clean animal but only one pair (two) of every unclean animal into the ark. See Genesis 7:2.
questions.p: God tell Noah make e carry seven-seven pair of clean animal, but for unclean animal, na only one pair (two) e go carry enter ark. Genesis 7:2 explain am well.

questions.q: Why did God confuse the language of the people and scatter them during the building of the tower of Babel?
o: Because they wanted to build a tower to reach into heaven and make a name for themselves in unity against Him
Because they had killed a prophet among them
Because they refused to have children and fill the earth
Because they refused to worship Him with sacrifices
questions.e: The people at Babel planned to build a city and tower to reach heaven so as to make a name for themselves and avoid being scattered; God confused their language and scattered them to stop their prideful unity. See Genesis 11:4-8.
questions.p: Di pipo for Babel wan build tower wey go reach heaven so dem go get famous name and no go scatter. God confuse dia language scatter dem so dat dia proud plan no go work. Genesis 11:4-8 talk am.

questions.q: What name did Eve give to the son God gave her as a replacement after Cain killed Abel?
o: Lamech
Methuselah
Seth
Enosh
questions.e: After Abel's death, Eve bore another son and named him Seth, saying God had appointed her another offspring instead of Abel. See Genesis 4:25.
questions.p: After Abel don die, Eve born anoda son and call am Seth, she talk say na God give am dis pikin instead of Abel. Genesis 4:25 explain am.

questions.q: According to Genesis chapter 9, what sign did God give Noah as a seal of His covenant never to destroy the earth again by flood?
o: An ark of wood
A pillar of fire
A burning bush
A rainbow in the sky
questions.e: God set the rainbow in the clouds as a sign of His covenant with Noah and every living creature. This is recorded in Genesis 9:12-13.
questions.p: God put rainbow for sky as sign of im covenant with Noah. Na for Genesis 9:12-13 dem write am.

questions.q: God commanded Abraham to practice circumcision as the sign of His covenant with him. According to Genesis 17, on which part of the body was this sign to be performed?
o: The hand
The ear
The flesh of the foreskin
The forehead
questions.e: God told Abraham that every male among his household should be circumcised in the flesh of the foreskin as a sign of the covenant. This is found in Genesis 17:10-11.
questions.p: God tell Abraham say make every man for im house cut dia foreskin as sign of di covenant. Na Genesis 17:10-11 talk am.

questions.q: At Mount Sinai, through whom did God give the Ten Commandments to the Israelites as part of the covenant relationship?
o: Moses
Caleb
Aaron
Joshua
questions.e: God called Moses up to Mount Sinai and gave him the Ten Commandments as the terms of the covenant for the Israelites. This is recorded in Exodus chapter 20.
questions.p: God call Moses go top Mount Sinai give am di Ten Commandments for di Israelites. Na Exodus chapter 20 tok am.

questions.q: In the covenant God made with Abraham in Genesis 15, what did God use to illustrate how numerous Abraham's descendants would become?
o: The dust of the ground
The stars of the sky
The sand of the sea
The leaves of the trees
questions.e: God brought Abraham outside and told him to count the stars if he could, saying his offspring would be just as numerous. This promise is recorded in Genesis 15:5.
questions.p: God carry Abraham commot, show am star for sky, tell am say im pikin dem go plenty like dat. Na Genesis 15:5 talk am.

questions.q: Before giving the Ten Commandments, God told the Israelites at Sinai that if they obeyed His voice and kept His covenant, they would become a special possession among all nations and also be called by what title, according to Exodus 19?
o: A land of milk and honey
A nation of warriors and kings
A chosen company of prophets
A kingdom of priests and a holy nation
questions.e: God promised that if Israel obeyed and kept the covenant, they would be His treasured possession, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. This condition is stated in Exodus 19:5-6.
questions.p: God tell Israel say if dem obey and keep di covenant, dem go be im special property, kingdom of priest and holy nation. Na Exodus 19:5-6 tok am.

questions.q: After the flood, God told Noah that He would never again use a flood to destroy all living creatures. This promise shows that the Noahic covenant was primarily an expression of God's what towards creation?
o: Punishment
Mercy and preservation
Wealth
Judgement
questions.e: God's promise not to destroy the earth by flood again shows His mercy and commitment to preserve life on earth despite human sin. This is seen in Genesis 9:11, where God binds Himself to this promise.
questions.p: God promise say e no go use flood destroy world again, dis show say e get mercy and e wan preserve life. Na Genesis 9:11 talk am.

questions.q: Comparing the covenant God made with Abraham and the covenant He made with Israel at Sinai, a key difference is that the Abrahamic covenant was based mainly on God's unconditional promise, while the Sinai covenant required the Israelites to do what in order to enjoy its blessings?
o: Obey God's laws and commandments
Conquer all neighbouring nations
Offer human sacrifices
Build a temple first
questions.e: Unlike the promise-based covenant with Abraham, the Sinai covenant was conditional, requiring Israel's obedience to God's laws to enjoy the covenant blessings, as stated in Exodus 19:5. Abraham's covenant depended on God's faithfulness, while Sinai depended also on Israel's response.
questions.p: Di covenant wey God make with Abraham na promise wey no get condition, but di one for Sinai need say Israel go obey God laws before dem go enjoy di blessing, as Exodus 19:5 talk am. Na di obedience be di difference.

questions.q: Abraham was circumcised as a sign that he accepted God's covenant. According to Genesis 17:24, how old was Abraham when this circumcision took place?
o: 120 years old
75 years old
86 years old
99 years old
questions.e: The Bible specifically records that Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in obedience to God's covenant command. This detail is found in Genesis 17:24.
questions.p: Bible tok clear say Abraham na ninety-nine years old when dem circumcise am as e obey God covenant. Na Genesis 17:24 get dis detail.

questions.q: According to Genesis, Joseph was how many years old when he stood before Pharaoh and began to serve as governor over Egypt?
o: 40 years old
35 years old
30 years old
25 years old
questions.e: The Bible records that Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and began his work of managing Egypt's affairs. This is found in Genesis 41:46.
questions.p: Bible talk say Joseph na thirty years old when e stand before Pharaoh begin manage Egypt matter. Dis dey for Genesis 41:46.

questions.q: For how many pieces of silver did Joseph's brothers sell him to the Ishmaelite merchants on their way to Egypt?
o: 30 pieces of silver
15 pieces of silver
20 pieces of silver
10 pieces of silver
questions.e: Joseph's brothers sold him to the Ishmaelite traders for twenty pieces of silver, as recorded in Genesis 37:28. This act of betrayal later led to Joseph's rise in Egypt.
questions.p: Joseph brothers sell am for twenty pieces of silver give the Ishmaelite traders, as e dey Genesis 37:28. Dis betrayal na wetin later make Joseph rise for Egypt.

questions.q: When baby Moses was placed in a basket and set afloat on the River Nile, who found and rescued him?
o: Pharaoh's wife
Zipporah, his future wife
Miriam, his sister
Pharaoh's daughter
questions.e: Exodus 2:5 tells us that Pharaoh's daughter came down to bathe at the river, saw the basket, and had it brought to her, thereby rescuing baby Moses. His sister Miriam was watching nearby and arranged for their mother to nurse him.
questions.p: Exodus 2:5 talk say na Pharaoh daughter come bathe for river, she see the basket come carry am, so she save baby Moses. Im sister Miriam dey watch from far come arrange say their mama go breastfeed am.

questions.q: Among the twelve men Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan, which two gave a good report of confidence that Israel could conquer the land?
o: Caleb and Joshua
Joshua and Aaron
Caleb and Othniel
Caleb and Phinehas
questions.e: Numbers 14:6-9 records that only Joshua and Caleb, out of the twelve spies, trusted God's promise and urged the people not to fear the inhabitants of Canaan. The other ten spies brought a discouraging report.
questions.p: Numbers 14:6-9 show say na only Joshua and Caleb, out of the twelve spy, trust God promise come tell the people make dem no fear the people wey dey Canaan. The remaining ten spy bring bad report wey discourage the people.

questions.q: Which woman served as a judge and prophetess in Israel, and led the nation to victory over Sisera and the army of Jabin, king of Canaan?
o: Huldah
Deborah
Miriam
Jael
questions.e: Judges 4 records that Deborah was a prophetess and judge of Israel who, together with Barak, led Israel to defeat Sisera's army. She held court under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel.
questions.p: Judges 4 talk say Deborah na prophetess and judge for Israel wey, together with Barak, lead Israel win Sisera army. She dey sit under palm tree between Ramah and Bethel judge people.

questions.q: Before Gideon attacked the Midianites, God reduced his army from 32,000 to 300 men. What test did God use to select the final 300 men at the water?
o: Those who refused to drink at all
Those who knelt down fully to drink
Those who lapped water with their tongue like a dog
Those who carried torches while drinking
questions.e: Judges 7:5-7 explains that God told Gideon to separate the men who lapped water with their tongue like a dog, putting their hand to their mouth, from those who knelt down to drink. The 300 who lapped were chosen to fight.
questions.p: Judges 7:5-7 explain say God tell Gideon make e separate the men wey lap water with their tongue like dog, wey put hand for mouth, from those wey kneel down drink. Na the 300 wey lap water God choose fight.

questions.q: During the conquest of Jericho under Joshua's leadership, how many times did the Israelites march around the city on the seventh day before its walls collapsed?
o: Twelve times
Once only
Three times
Seven times
questions.e: Joshua 6:15-16 records that on the seventh day, the Israelites marched around Jericho seven times, and after the seventh time, the priests blew the trumpets and the walls fell down flat. On the other six days they had marched around only once.
questions.p: Joshua 6:15-16 talk say for the seventh day, Israel people match round Jericho seven times, and after the seventh time, the priests blow trumpet make the wall fall flat. For the other six days na only once dem dey match round am.

questions.q: During the wilderness journey, what visible sign did God use to guide the Israelites by day and by night respectively?
o: A rainbow by day and a bright star by night
A pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night
A bright star by day and a burning bush by night
A flock of eagles by day and a pillar of smoke by night
questions.e: God led the Israelites with a pillar of cloud during the day to guide them and a pillar of fire at night to give them light, showing His constant guidance. This is recorded in Exodus 13:21.
questions.p: God yan use cloud pillar guide dem for daytime and fire pillar for night time. E be like say God dey show say He dey always lead dem. Dis dey Exodus 13:21.

questions.q: God provided bread from heaven called manna for the Israelites in the wilderness. On which day of the week were they told not to go out to gather it because none would fall?
o: The seventh day (Sabbath)
The first day
The sixth day
The third day
questions.e: God commanded that no manna would fall on the seventh day, the Sabbath, because the people had gathered a double portion the day before. This taught them to rest and trust God's provision, as recorded in Exodus 16:26.
questions.p: God talk say manna no go fall for seventh day wey be Sabbath, because dem don already gather double portion the day before. Dis teach dem to rest and trust God, Exodus 16:26.

questions.q: Besides manna, God also provided meat for the Israelites to eat in the wilderness. What kind of bird covered the camp in the evening for this purpose?
o: Sparrows
Doves
Quails
Pigeons
questions.e: In the evening, quails came up and covered the camp, giving the Israelites meat to eat alongside the manna that fell in the morning. This shows God's full provision for their needs, as seen in Exodus 16:13.
questions.p: For evening time, quails come cover the camp give dem meat chop, join the manna wey dey fall for morning. Na God dey provide everything dem need, Exodus 16:13.

questions.q: When Pharaoh's army pursued the Israelites to the Red Sea, God made a way of escape for them. What natural means did God use to divide the sea so they could cross on dry ground?
o: A sudden earthquake
A thick fog that confused the Egyptians
A heavy downpour of rain
A strong east wind blowing all night
questions.e: God sent a strong east wind that blew all night, driving the sea back and making the waters stand like walls so the Israelites could walk through on dry ground. This great act of protection is recorded in Exodus 14:21.
questions.p: God send strong east wind wey blow throughout the night, e push the sea back make water stand like wall so Israelites fit waka pass for dry ground. Na big protection, Exodus 14:21.

questions.q: At Marah, the Israelites found water but could not drink it because it was bitter. What did Moses do, as instructed by God, to make the water sweet and drinkable?
o: He prayed and poured oil into the water
He threw a piece of wood into the water
He sprinkled salt into the water
He struck the water with his staff
questions.e: God showed Moses a piece of wood, and when he threw it into the bitter water at Marah, the water became sweet and fit to drink. This miracle demonstrated God's care in providing good water for His people, as found in Exodus 15:23-25.
questions.p: God show Moses one wood, when e throw am inside the bitter water for Marah, the water sweet come fit drink. Dis miracle show say God dey care for Im people, Exodus 15:23-25.

questions.q: During the battle between Israel and the Amalekites, Moses stood on a hill with his hands raised, and as long as he held them up, Israel prevailed. Who helped to hold up his tired hands so Israel could win the battle?
o: Aaron and Hur
Eleazar and Ithamar
Joshua and Caleb
Nadab and Abihu
questions.e: When Moses grew tired, Aaron and Hur held up his hands on both sides until sunset, which helped Israel to defeat the Amalekites. This shows how God used human cooperation alongside His divine power to protect His people, as recorded in Exodus 17:11-12.
questions.p: When Moses hand tire, Aaron and Hur hold im hand up from both sides till sun set, and e help Israel win the Amalekites. God use human effort join im power to protect im people, Exodus 17:11-12.

questions.q: When fiery serpents bit many Israelites in the wilderness because of their complaints, God told Moses to make a bronze serpent and put it on a pole. What did a bitten person need to do in order to be healed?
o: Touch the pole with their right hand
Look at the bronze serpent
Drink water mixed with ashes from the serpent
Offer a lamb as sacrifice immediately
questions.e: God instructed that anyone bitten by a serpent who looked at the bronze serpent on the pole would live. This act of faith in looking brought healing and protection from death, as recorded in Numbers 21:8-9.
questions.p: God talk say anybody wey snake bite, if e look the bronze snake wey dey the pole, e go live. Na faith to look bring healing and protection from death, Numbers 21:8-9.

questions.q: In the Bible story of Samuel's birth, who was the woman that prayed earnestly at Shiloh and vowed to dedicate her son to God's service if she had a child?
o: Hannah
Abigail
Deborah
Miriam
questions.e: Hannah was barren and prayed at Shiloh, promising to give her son to the Lord. God answered her prayer and she had Samuel. This is recorded in 1 Samuel 1:10-20.
questions.p: Hannah na the woman wey no get pikin, she pray for Shiloh say if she born pikin she go give am to God. God hear her prayer, she born Samuel. Dis dey for 1 Samuel 1:10-20.

questions.q: After Samuel was weaned, his mother took him to the house of the Lord to live and serve. Who was the priest in charge there at that time?
o: Samuel
Ahimelech
Zadok
Eli
questions.e: Hannah brought young Samuel to Eli the priest at Shiloh, where the boy grew up ministering before the Lord. This is found in 1 Samuel 1:24-28.
questions.p: Hannah carry small Samuel go met Eli di priest for Shiloh, na dia e grow dey serve God. Dis one dey 1 Samuel 1:24-28.

questions.q: On the night God first called Samuel, the boy ran to his guardian three times thinking he had been summoned by him. Who did Samuel mistakenly think was calling him?
o: Phinehas
His father Elkanah
Eli
Hophni
questions.e: God called Samuel at night, but because Samuel was not yet familiar with God's voice, he ran to Eli three times before Eli realised it was the Lord calling. This is in 1 Samuel 3:1-9.
questions.p: God call Samuel for night but Samuel no sabi na God dey call am, so e run go meet Eli three times. Na Eli later realise say na God dey call am. E dey 1 Samuel 3:1-9.

questions.q: What wrongdoing did Eli's sons, Hophni and Phinehas, commit at the tabernacle which angered God against Eli's household?
o: They refused to offer sacrifices at all
They stole the ark of the covenant and sold it
They worshipped idols openly in the temple
They took the best portions of sacrificial meat for themselves and committed immorality with women at the entrance of the tent of meeting
questions.e: Hophni and Phinehas abused their priestly office by seizing choice meat meant for God before it was offered and by sleeping with women who served at the tabernacle entrance. This corruption is described in 1 Samuel 2:12-17 and 22.
questions.p: Hophni and Phinehas dey collect di better meat wey suppose go God before dem offer am, dem sef dey sleep with women wey dey serve for tabernacle gate. Dis bad bad tin dey 1 Samuel 2:12-17 and 22.

questions.q: God rebuked Eli for failing in his parental duty concerning his wicked sons. What exactly was Eli's fault as a father, according to the account?
o: He encouraged his sons to leave the priesthood
He gave all his wealth to his sons instead of to God
He knew of his sons' sins but only mildly rebuked them without restraining them
He disowned his sons publicly
questions.e: Eli was aware that his sons were sinning greatly but only spoke weak words of caution and did not stop them, honouring his sons above God. This failure of parental discipline brought judgement on his house, as shown in 1 Samuel 2:22-25 and 2:29.
questions.p: Eli sabi say im children dey do bad but im just dey warn dem small small, e no stop dem well well. Because e honour im pikin pass God, judgement come fall on im house. Dis dey 1 Samuel 2:22-25 and 2:29.

questions.q: As a consequence of Eli's failure to restrain his sons, what tragic event happened to Hophni and Phinehas in a battle against the Philistines?
o: They both repented and became priests of the Lord again
They both died on the same day and the ark of God was captured
They escaped to Egypt and lived in exile
They were made kings over Israel
questions.e: In the battle at Aphek, the Israelites were defeated, Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the ark of the covenant was captured by the Philistines, fulfilling God's judgement on Eli's house. This is recorded in 1 Samuel 4:10-11.
questions.p: Dem fight war for Aphek, Israel lose, Hophni and Phinehas die di same day, and di ark of God enter enemy hand. Na dis God warning come pass for 1 Samuel 4:10-11.

questions.q: When God sent Samuel to anoint a new king from the sons of Jesse in Bethlehem, what important lesson did God teach Samuel about choosing a leader?
o: That man looks at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart
That the tallest and strongest son should always be chosen
That wealth and family status determine God's choice
That only the firstborn son could be anointed king
questions.e: When Samuel was impressed by Eliab's appearance, God corrected him, saying that people judge by looks but God judges the heart, leading to David, the youngest shepherd boy, being chosen. This teaching is in 1 Samuel 16:6-7.
questions.p: Wen Samuel see Eliab e tink say na im be di one, but God tell am say human dey check outside, but God dey check inside heart. Na so David, di small boy wey dey herd sheep, come dey chosen. E dey 1 Samuel 16:6-7.

questions.q: Before he was anointed king, what was David's main occupation when Samuel came to his father's house in Bethlehem?
o: He was a soldier in Saul's army
He was tending his father's sheep in the field
He was a farmer growing wheat
He was studying under the prophets in Ramah
questions.e: David was the youngest son and was out keeping the sheep when Samuel came to Jesse's house, so he was sent for and anointed. This is found in 1 Samuel 16:11-13.
questions.p: David na di last born and e dey bush dey herd sheep wen Samuel come to dia house, dem send person go call am, dem come anoint am. Dis one dey 1 Samuel 16:11-13.

questions.q: In the Bible, who anointed Saul to become the first king of Israel?
o: Samuel
Gad
Nathan
Eli
questions.e: Samuel, the prophet and judge, anointed Saul with oil and declared him ruler over Israel. This event is recorded in 1 Samuel 10:1.
questions.p: Samuel na the prophet wey pour oil for Saul head make him be king. Na for 1 Samuel 10:1 e dey.

questions.q: God commanded Saul through Samuel to completely destroy the Amalekites and all their possessions, including livestock. What did Saul do instead?
o: He killed everyone and everything as instructed
He spared King Agag and kept the best sheep and cattle
He gave all the animals to the Levites
He refused to fight the Amalekites
questions.e: Saul disobeyed God's clear command by sparing Agag and keeping the best animals, claiming they were for sacrifice. This disobedience is recorded in 1 Samuel 15:9.
questions.p: Saul no obey wetin God talk; instead e spare Agag and the best animals, e no kill everything. Na dis one dey 1 Samuel 15:9.

questions.q: What was the main reason God rejected Saul as king over Israel?
o: Saul was too young to rule
Saul lost a major battle against the Philistines
Saul disobeyed God's instructions regarding the Amalekites
Saul refused to marry Michal
questions.e: Saul's disobedience in sparing Agag and the best livestock, against God's direct command, led to his rejection as king. Samuel told him that obedience is better than sacrifice in 1 Samuel 15:22-23.

questions.q: Before his final battle against the Philistines, Saul disobeyed God's law by consulting whom for guidance?

The prophet Elijah
The high priest Abiathar
The medium at Endor

questions.q: Samuel told Saul that 'to obey is better than sacrifice.' What important lesson does this statement teach?

Kings are exempted from offering sacrifices
Sacrifices are no longer necessary in worship
Sacrifices should only be offered by priests, not kings
questions.e: Samuel's statement teaches that true devotion to God is shown through obedience to His word, not just through outward religious acts like sacrifice. Saul had sacrificed animals but disobeyed God's specific command, showing his heart was not right. This is found in 1 Samuel 15:22.
questions.p: Samuel talk say to obey God pass to just dey offer sacrifice. E dey show say wetin God want na your obedience, no be only outside show of religion. Na 1 Samuel 15:22.

questions.q: David's sin involving Bathsheba led him to arrange the death of which man in battle?

Nabal
Abner
Uriah the Hittite

questions.p: David commit adultery with Bathsheba and e arrange make dem kill her husband Uriah for war to cover im sin. Na for 2 Samuel 11.

questions.q: Despite his father Saul's hatred and jealousy toward David, which of Saul's sons remained a loyal and faithful friend to David?

Jonathan
Ishbosheth
Abinadab

questions.p: Jonathan, Saul pikin, love David well well and e protect am from Saul anger, even though na im papa. Na for 1 Samuel 18:1-3 and 1 Samuel 20 e dey.

questions.q: After David became king, what act of disobedience to God did he commit that led to a plague on Israel?

He refused to bring the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem
He conducted a census of Israel without God's approval
He built an altar to foreign gods
questions.e: David ordered a census of the fighting men of Israel, an act that displeased God, possibly because it showed pride in military strength rather than trust in God. As a result, a plague struck Israel, killing many people, as recorded in 2 Samuel 24.
questions.p: David count the fighting men of Israel without God approval, e be like say e dey trust im army strength instead of God. Na so plague come kill many people, na for 2 Samuel 24.

questions.q: In the Bible, which young shepherd from Bethlehem defeated the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and a stone?

David
Solomon
Saul

questions.q: When God offered Solomon anything he wished for at the start of his reign, what did Solomon specifically request?

Long life
Victory over his enemies
Wisdom to judge the people well
questions.e: Solomon asked God for an understanding heart to judge Israel rightly instead of asking for riches or long life. God was pleased and gave him wisdom plus riches and honour as a bonus. This is recorded in 1 Kings 3:5-14.
questions.p: Solomon no ask for money or long life, e ask God for wisdom make e fit judge Israel well. God happy and e give am wisdom plus riches and honour on top. Dis story dey 1 Kings 3:5-14.

questions.q: King David committed a grave sin by taking another man's wife and then arranging for the woman's husband to die in battle. What was the name of this loyal soldier whom David had killed?

Amasa
Abner
Joab
questions.e: David took Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite, and then arranged for Uriah to be killed in battle to hide his sin. This story is recorded in 2 Samuel 11.
questions.p: David take Bathsheba, wey be Uriah the Hittite wife, then e arrange make dem kill Uriah for war so e fit hide im sin. Dis one dey 2 Samuel 11.

questions.q: Which prophet was sent by God to confront King David over his sin involving Bathsheba, using a parable about a poor man's only lamb?

Samuel
Nathan
Elijah
questions.e: Nathan the prophet told David a parable about a rich man who took a poor man's only lamb, which made David realise and confess his own sin against Uriah and Bathsheba. This confrontation is found in 2 Samuel 12.
questions.p: Prophet Nathan tell David parable about one rich man wey take poor man im only lamb, and David come realise say na im dey do dat kind sin. Dis confrontation dey 2 Samuel 12.

questions.q: Which great structure in Jerusalem did King Solomon build as the most notable achievement of his reign, fulfilling his father David's desire?
o: The city wall
The royal palace
The ark of the covenant
The Temple of the Lord
questions.e: Solomon built the magnificent Temple in Jerusalem, fulfilling what David had wished to do but was not permitted by God to carry out. The building of the Temple is described in 1 Kings 6.
questions.p: Solomon build the fine Temple for Jerusalem, wey be wetin David wan do but God no gree am do am. Dem describe how dem build di Temple for 1 Kings 6.

questions.q: Which of King David's own sons rebelled against him and temporarily seized the throne, forcing David to flee Jerusalem?

Solomon
Adonijah
Amnon

questions.q: Despite his great wisdom, King Solomon's reign ended with a serious spiritual failure that provoked God's anger. What was this failure?

He married many foreign wives who turned his heart to worship other gods
He refused to build the Temple
He gave away the ark of the covenant
questions.e: Solomon married many foreign women, and in his old age they turned his heart away from the Lord to worship idols, which angered God greatly. This failure is recorded in 1 Kings 11.
questions.p: Solomon marry plenty foreign wives, and as e dey old, dem turn im mind comot from God go idol worship, wey vex God well well. Dis failure dey 1 Kings 11.

questions.q: After King Solomon died, who succeeded him as king of Judah before the kingdom split into two?

Jeroboam
Rehoboam
Abijah

questions.q: Before he became king of the northern tribes, Jeroboam held what position under King Solomon?

High priest in Jerusalem
Commander of the royal army
Governor of Judah

questions.p: Jeroboam na strong young man wey Solomon put to oversee the forced labour for house of Joseph. E dey written for 1 Kings 11:28.

questions.q: At which town did the Israelites gather to make Rehoboam king and to demand a lighter burden before the kingdom divided?

Bethel
Shiloh
Shechem
questions.e: All Israel assembled at Shechem to crown Rehoboam, and there they asked him to lighten the heavy yoke his father Solomon had placed on them. This is in 1 Kings 12:1.
questions.p: All Israel gather for Shechem to crown Rehoboam, and na there dem beg am make e lighten the heavy load wey Solomon put on dem. E dey 1 Kings 12:1.

questions.q: Whose advice did Rehoboam follow when he decided to answer the people harshly, promising to make their burden even heavier?
o: The advice of the prophet Ahijah
The advice of the young men who grew up with him
The advice of his mother, Naamah
The advice of the elders who served Solomon
questions.e: Rehoboam rejected the gentle counsel of the elders and instead followed the young men who grew up with him, telling the people he would be harsher than his father. This led to the split, as told in 1 Kings 12:8-14.
questions.p: Rehoboam no listen to the old men wey serve Solomon, instead e follow the young men wey grow with am, wey tell am to dey harsh pass im papa. Na so the kingdom split, as e dey 1 Kings 12:8-14.

questions.q: How many tribes of Israel broke away from Rehoboam to follow Jeroboam, forming the northern kingdom of Israel?

Two
Twelve
Seven
questions.e: Ten tribes rebelled and followed Jeroboam, while only Judah and Benjamin remained loyal to Rehoboam. This is recorded in 1 Kings 11:31-35 and 1 Kings 12:20.
questions.p: Ten tribes rebel follow Jeroboam, na only Judah and Benjamin remain with Rehoboam. E dey 1 Kings 11:31-35 and 1 Kings 12:20.

questions.q: Why did Jeroboam set up two golden calves at Bethel and Dan for the people of Israel to worship?
o: To please the king of Egypt who had sheltered him
To stop the people from going to Jerusalem to worship and returning their loyalty to Rehoboam
To fulfil a vow he made before becoming king
To honour the memory of Moses and Aaron
questions.e: Jeroboam feared that if the people kept going to the temple in Jerusalem to worship, their hearts would turn back to Rehoboam and he might be killed. So he made golden calves at Bethel and Dan as alternative worship centres. This is in 1 Kings 12:26-29.
questions.p: Jeroboam fear say if people continue to dey go Jerusalem temple to worship, dem go turn back their heart to Rehoboam and e fit kill am. So e make golden calves for Bethel and Dan make dem fit worship there instead. E dey 1 Kings 12:26-29.

questions.q: Which officer did Rehoboam send to the rebellious Israelites, who was stoned to death by the people?
o: Ahijah the prophet
Hadad the Edomite
Adoram, who was over the forced labour
Shemaiah the prophet
questions.e: Rehoboam sent Adoram, the officer in charge of forced labour, to deal with Israel, but the people stoned him to death, showing their deep anger over forced labour. Rehoboam then fled to Jerusalem. This is recorded in 1 Kings 12:18.
questions.p: Rehoboam send Adoram, the officer wey dey over forced labour, go meet Israel, but the people stone am die, wey show say dem vex well for the forced labour matter. Rehoboam quick run go Jerusalem. E dey 1 Kings 12:18.

questions.q: Which prophet told Rehoboam and the men of Judah not to go to war against their brothers in Israel after the kingdom split?
o: Nathan
Gad
Elijah
Shemaiah
questions.e: When Rehoboam gathered an army to fight Israel and reunite the kingdom, the prophet Shemaiah told him that the division was from God and he should not fight his brothers. Rehoboam obeyed and sent the army home. This is found in 1 Kings 12:21-24.

Jehoshaphat
Omri
Ahab

River Jabbok
Brook Cherith
River Jordan

questions.p: God tell Elijah make e hide for Brook Cherith, east side of Jordan, and ravens dey bring am food during di hunger wey come because of Ahab idol worship. E dey for 1 Kings 17:2-6.

questions.q: On Mount Carmel, Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal to a contest by fire to prove who the true God was. How many prophets of Baal did Elijah confront and later kill at the brook Kishon?

Blindness
Deafness
Paralysis

Five times
Three times
Seven times

questions.p: Elisha tell Naaman make e go wash for Jordan river seven times, and after e do am, im skin come clean like small pikin own. E dey for 2 Kings 5:10, 5:14.

Gehazi
Jehu
Obadiah

Adultery with a palace servant
Theft from the royal treasury
Murder of a fellow Israelite
questions.e: Jezebel hired two false witnesses to testify that Naboth had cursed God and the king, a crime punishable by stoning, so that Ahab could unjustly take his vineyard after his death. This is recorded in 1 Kings 21:10-13.

Mount Carmel
Mount Horeb
Mount Gilboa

An altar dedicated to Baal

Elijah

Marriage must always be monogamous

Rebuild the fallen tabernacle of David

questions.p: Jesus talk say, 'whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment' (Matthew 5:22). E dey show say the mind wey get anger fit cause serious judgment just like action wey person do.

questions.q: In the parable of the wise and foolish builders at the end of the Sermon on the Mount, what key lesson does Jesus pass across about the man who built his house on rock?
o: Wealthy people build better houses than poor people
Strong building materials guarantee safety
Hearing and obeying Jesus' words gives a person a stable foundation for life
Good location always prevents disaster
questions.e: Jesus said whoever hears His sayings and does them is like a wise man who built on rock, and the house stood firm when storms came (Matthew 7:24-25). The parable teaches that obedience to Christ's teaching, not physical factors, gives true stability in life.
questions.p: Jesus talk say whoever hear im word and do am na like wise man wey build house for rock, and the house stand strong when storm come (Matthew 7:24-25). The parable dey teach say na to obey Christ word dey give person correct foundation for life, no be physical thing.

questions.q: Jesus taught about two gates and two paths in Matthew chapter 7. What does the wide gate and broad way represent in this teaching?
o: The path that leads to eternal life
The path of self-denial and sacrifice
The path followed by the righteous few
The path that leads to destruction
questions.e: Jesus said, 'wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat' (Matthew 7:13). The contrast is with the narrow gate that leads to life, which few find, teaching that the easier popular path is spiritually dangerous.
questions.p: Jesus talk say, 'wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat' (Matthew 7:13). E dey contrast am with narrow gate wey dey lead to life, wey na only small people dey find, e dey show say the popular easy road dey dangerous for soul.

questions.q: During the trial of Jesus, the Roman governor who asked the crowd, 'What shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?' and later washed his hands to show he was innocent of Jesus' blood was
o: Pontius Pilate
Caiaphas
Herod Antipas
Felix
questions.e: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor who tried Jesus, found no fault in Him, but gave in to the crowd's demand and washed his hands. This is recorded in Matthew 27:24.
questions.p: Na Pontius Pilate be di Roman governor wey judge Jesus. E no see wetin Jesus do wrong but e still gree hand Am over, so e wash hand to show say e no gilti. Matthew 27:24 talk am.

questions.q: On the way to Golgotha, the soldiers forced a passer-by from Cyrene to carry the cross of Jesus. What was this man's name?
o: Barnabas
Andrew
Simon
Lazarus
questions.e: Simon of Cyrene was compelled by the soldiers to carry the cross of Jesus to Golgotha. This event is recorded in Mark 15:21.
questions.p: Na Simon of Cyrene dem force make e carry Jesus cross go Golgotha. Mark 15:21 tell us dis story.

questions.q: After Jesus died, a rich member of the Jewish council who had secretly believed in Him went to Pilate to request His body for burial. Who was this man?
o: Simeon
Gamaliel
Nicodemus
Joseph of Arimathea
questions.e: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member, asked Pilate for Jesus' body and buried it in his own new tomb. This is recorded in Matthew 27:57-60.
questions.p: Joseph of Arimathea, wey be big man for di Jewish council, go beg Pilate make e give am Jesus body so e fit bury Am for im own new tomb. Matthew 27:57-60 talk am.

questions.q: On the morning of the resurrection, the person who first saw the risen Jesus and was sent to tell the other disciples was
o: Mary Magdalene
John
Thomas
Peter
questions.e: Mary Magdalene was the first to see the risen Jesus near the empty tomb, and He instructed her to go and tell the disciples. This is recorded in John 20:14-18.
questions.p: Mary Magdalene na di first person wey see Jesus after e resurrect, near di empty tomb. Jesus tell am make e go tell di oda disciples. John 20:14-18 talk am.

questions.q: One disciple refused to believe that Jesus had risen until he could see and touch the nail prints in Jesus' hands and side. Who was this disciple?
o: James
Thomas
Philip
Bartholomew
questions.e: Thomas doubted the resurrection until he personally saw and touched Jesus' wounds, after which he confessed, 'My Lord and my God.' This is recorded in John 20:24-28.
questions.p: Thomas no gree believe say Jesus don resurrect until e see and touch di wound for Jesus hand and side. Afta dat e talk say 'My Lord and my God.' John 20:24-28 talk am.

questions.q: At the exact moment Jesus died on the cross, a significant event happened in the temple that symbolised that access to God was now open to all people. What was this event?
o: The priests fled from the temple
The veil of the temple was torn in two
The temple was destroyed by fire
The ark of the covenant disappeared
questions.e: At the moment Jesus died, the veil of the temple separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place was torn from top to bottom, symbolising direct access to God through Jesus. This is recorded in Matthew 27:51.
questions.p: Di moment wey Jesus die, di curtain wey dey separate di Holy Place from di Most Holy Place for temple tear from up reach down. Dis one show say people fit now come near God through Jesus. Matthew 27:51 talk am.

questions.q: Just before His ascension, Jesus led His disciples out to a particular location near Jerusalem where He gave them final instructions and was then taken up into heaven. Where was this place?
o: Mount Sinai
Mount Gerizim
Mount of Olives
Mount Carmel
questions.e: Jesus led His disciples to the Mount of Olives, near Bethany, where He blessed them and was taken up into heaven while they watched. This is recorded in Luke 24:50-51 and Acts 1:9-12.
questions.p: Jesus carry Im disciples go Mount of Olives, near Bethany, where e bless dem and den dem see Am as e dey rise go heaven. Luke 24:50-51 and Acts 1:9-12 talk am.

questions.q: On the Day of Pentecost, what visible sign accompanied the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the disciples as they gathered together in Jerusalem?
o: Tongues of fire resting on each of them
Thick darkness covering the city
A dove descending from heaven
A bright star appearing over the house
questions.e: The Bible says divided tongues like fire appeared and rested on each disciple, and they began to speak in other tongues. This is recorded in Acts 2:3.
questions.p: Bible talk say tongue of fire come rest for everybody head, and dem start to speak different languages. Dis one dey for Acts 2:3.

questions.q: Who delivered the first public sermon to the crowd immediately after the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples at Pentecost?
o: John
Stephen
Philip
Peter
questions.e: Peter stood up with the eleven and explained to the crowd that what they were seeing was the fulfilment of Joel's prophecy. This sermon is found in Acts 2:14-36.
questions.p: Peter na im stand up with di eleven disciples come explain say na wetin Joel talk before dey happen. Dis one dey for Acts 2:14-36.

questions.q: According to the account in Acts, about how many people were added to the church on the day Peter preached at Pentecost?
questions.e: After Peter's sermon, those who believed his message were baptised and about three thousand souls were added that day. This number is recorded in Acts 2:41.
questions.p: After Peter preach, many pipo believe come baptise, and around three thousand pipo join dat day. E dey for Acts 2:41.

questions.q: Peter and John healed a man who was lame from birth as he begged for alms at which gate of the temple in Jerusalem?
o: The Beautiful Gate
The Golden Gate
The Water Gate
The Sheep Gate
questions.e: The lame man was sitting at the gate called Beautiful, asking for alms, when Peter healed him in the name of Jesus Christ. This is found in Acts 3:2-7.
questions.p: Dis lame man dey sidon for di gate wey dem call Beautiful Gate dey beg money, Peter come heal am for Jesus name. E dey for Acts 3:2-7.

questions.q: Who became the first Christian martyr after being stoned to death by an angry mob while Saul of Tarsus watched and approved?
o: James the son of Zebedee
Barnabas
Stephen
Philip the evangelist
questions.e: Stephen, a deacon full of faith and the Holy Spirit, was dragged out of the city and stoned to death for his testimony about Jesus. This event is recorded in Acts 7:58-60.
questions.p: Stephen, one deacon wey Holy Spirit full, na im dem stone kill for outside di city because of im testimony about Jesus. E dey for Acts 7:58-60.

questions.q: In his defence speech before the Sanhedrin, Stephen mainly traced which theme to show that the Jewish leaders had always resisted God?
o: The Jewish laws on clean and unclean foods
The history of Israel and their repeated rejection of God's messengers
Only the miracles performed by Moses in Egypt
The detailed genealogy of Jesus Christ
questions.e: Stephen reviewed Israel's history from Abraham through Moses to Solomon, showing a pattern where the people constantly resisted the Holy Spirit and rejected God's chosen messengers, as in Acts chapter 7.
questions.p: Stephen waka through Israel history from Abraham reach Solomon, e show say dem dey always resist Holy Spirit and reject God in-im messengers. Dis one dey for Acts chapter 7.

questions.q: Who was the young man who approved of Stephen's killing and kept watch over the garments of those who stoned him, later becoming a fierce persecutor of the church?
o: Barnabas
Ananias of Damascus
Saul of Tarsus
Gamaliel
questions.e: Acts 7:58 and 8:1 mention a young man named Saul who kept the clothes of those stoning Stephen and approved of his death; he later persecuted the church before his conversion.
questions.p: Acts 7:58 and 8:1 talk say young man wey dem call Saul dey hold di cloth of dose wey dey stone Stephen, and e support di killing before e later convert.

questions.q: After Stephen's death, a great persecution scattered believers from Jerusalem throughout Judea and Samaria. What was one major positive result of this scattering for the growth of the church?
o: The scattered believers preached the word wherever they went, spreading the gospel to new regions
All the apostles were killed and the church disappeared
Christianity was completely banned throughout the Roman Empire
The church in Jerusalem became the only true church and stopped growing
questions.e: Acts 8:1 and 8:4 show that although persecution scattered the believers, they did not stop preaching; instead they carried the gospel message to new places like Samaria, which helped the church grow beyond Jerusalem.
questions.p: Acts 8:1 and 8:4 show say even though persecution scatter di believers, dem no stop to preach; instead dem carry di gospel go new places like Samaria, and church grow pass Jerusalem.

questions.q: Before his dramatic conversion to Christianity, the apostle Paul was commonly known by what Hebrew name?
o: Stephen
Simon
Silas
Saul
questions.e: Paul was originally called Saul, a Pharisee who persecuted the early church before his conversion. After his conversion he became known as Paul. This is recorded in Acts 13:9.
questions.p: Before Paul convert, dem dey call am Saul, na Pharisee wey dey persecute church people. After e convert, dem begin call am Paul. E dey for Acts 13:9.

questions.q: On the road to which city did Saul see a bright light from heaven and hear the voice of Jesus, leading to his conversion?
o: Tarsus
Damascus
Antioch
Jerusalem
questions.e: Saul was travelling to Damascus to arrest Christians when a light from heaven shone around him and Jesus spoke to him. This encounter is found in Acts 9:3-4.
questions.p: Saul dey waka go Damascus to arrest Christians when light shine from heaven and Jesus talk to am. E dey for Acts 9:3-4.

questions.q: After Saul was struck blind on the road to Damascus, which disciple did God send to pray for him, restore his sight and baptize him?
o: Barnabas
Ananias
Timothy
Silas
questions.e: God sent Ananias, a disciple in Damascus, to lay hands on Saul so his sight could be restored and he could be filled with the Holy Spirit and baptized. This is recorded in Acts 9:10-18.
questions.p: God send Ananias, one disciple wey dey Damascus, to lay hand for Saul body make im eye open and im receive Holy Spirit and baptism. E dey for Acts 9:10-18.

questions.q: Who was sent out together with Paul by the church at Antioch to begin his first missionary journey?
o: Timothy
Silas
Titus
Barnabas
questions.e: The Holy Spirit instructed the church at Antioch to set apart Barnabas and Saul for missionary work, and they were sent out together. This is recorded in Acts 13:1-3.
questions.p: Holy Spirit talk make Antioch church separate Barnabas and Saul for mission work, and dem send dem together. E dey for Acts 13:1-3.

questions.q: What was the main issue that was debated at the Council of Jerusalem concerning Gentile believers?
o: Whether Gentiles should be circumcised and keep the law of Moses
Whether the Sabbath day should be completely abolished
Whether Paul should be arrested by the Roman authorities
Whether Peter should become the sole leader of the church
questions.e: Some believers from Judea taught that Gentile converts must be circumcised and keep the law of Moses to be saved, which caused a sharp dispute that was brought before the apostles and elders at Jerusalem. This is recorded in Acts 15:1-5.
questions.p: Some Jewish believers teach say Gentile converts must circumcise and keep Moses law before dem fit save, and dis cause plenty argument wey carry go apostles and elders for Jerusalem. E dey for Acts 15:1-5.

questions.q: At the end of the Council of Jerusalem, the apostles sent a letter to Gentile believers listing a few requirements. Which of the following was NOT included in that letter?
o: Abstain from food that has been polluted by idols
Abstain from meat of animals that have been strangled
Be circumcised according to the law of Moses
Abstain from blood
questions.e: The Jerusalem council decided that Gentiles did not need to be circumcised, but only asked them to avoid food offered to idols, blood, meat of strangled animals, and sexual immorality. Circumcision was deliberately left out of the requirements. This is recorded in Acts 15:28-29.
questions.p: Di council for Jerusalem decide say Gentiles no need circumcise, dem only tell dem make dem avoid food wey dem offer to idols, blood, meat of animal wey dem strangle, and sexual sin. Circumcision no dey inside di list at all. E dey for Acts 15:28-29.

questions.q: What trade or occupation did Paul practice to earn a living while carrying out his missionary work?
o: Fishing
Tentmaking
Carpentry
Farming
questions.e: Paul worked as a tentmaker alongside Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth, which allowed him to support himself financially during his ministry. This is recorded in Acts 18:3.
questions.p: Paul be tentmaker, e dey work together with Aquila and Priscilla for Corinth so e fit take care of imself financially while e dey do ministry. E dey for Acts 18:3.

questions.q: During the Council of Jerusalem, Peter argued strongly that Gentile believers should not be forced to keep the law of Moses. What was the main basis of his argument?
o: Paul had threatened to leave the church if the law was imposed on Gentiles
The law of Moses had already been officially abolished by the Roman government
Gentiles had already received the Holy Spirit just as the Jewish believers did
Gentiles were generally wealthier and more influential than Jewish believers
questions.e: Peter reminded the council that God had already shown approval of the Gentiles by giving them the Holy Spirit just as He did to the Jews, without requiring them to keep the law first, proving that salvation is through grace. This reasoning is found in Acts 15:7-11.
questions.p: Peter remind di council say God don already show say e accept Gentiles because e give dem Holy Spirit just like e give di Jews, without make dem keep law first, dis show say salvation na through grace. Dis reasoning dey for Acts 15:7-11.

questions.q: According to Romans 5:1, what do believers obtain with God as a result of being justified by faith?
o: Peace with God
Authority over nations
Wealth and honour
Long life on earth
questions.e: Romans 5:1 says, 'Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.' Justification by faith restores a right relationship with God, bringing peace, not material gain.
questions.p: Romans 5:1 talk say, 'Now wey dem don justify us through faith, we get peace with God through Jesus Christ.' E no talk about money or power, na peace with God dem get.

questions.q: In 1 Corinthians 13:13, Paul lists faith, hope and love as things that remain, but which one does he say is the greatest?
o: Wisdom
Faith
Hope
Love
questions.e: 1 Corinthians 13:13 clearly states that faith, hope and love remain, 'but the greatest of these is love.' This shows love as the supreme Christian virtue above faith and hope.
questions.p: 1 Corinthians 13:13 talk say faith, hope and love dey remain, but love pass dem all. So love na the greatest among the three.

questions.q: According to 1 Corinthians 12:7, for what purpose did the Holy Spirit give different spiritual gifts to believers?
o: For the common good of all believers
For material wealth
For personal pride
For political influence
questions.e: 1 Corinthians 12:7 says, 'the manifestation of the Spirit is given to each one for the profit of all.' Spiritual gifts are meant to benefit the whole church body, not individual gain.
questions.p: 1 Corinthians 12:7 talk say the Spirit dey show himself for everybody good, not for one person alone. So spiritual gifts na for help everybody for church, no be for pride or money.

questions.q: According to Galatians 3:24, what role did the law play before the coming of Christ?
o: It condemned believers forever
It replaced the need for grace
It served as a tutor to lead people to Christ
It saved all who obeyed it perfectly
questions.e: Galatians 3:24 says, 'the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.' The law prepared people to recognise their need for a Saviour.
questions.p: Galatians 3:24 talk say the law be like teacher wey dey guide people go meet Christ, so dat faith go justify dem. The law no be final solution, na preparation for Christ.

questions.q: According to Romans 3:23, what have all human beings done, making them fall short of the glory of God?
o: Refused to build temples
Rejected the law of Moses
Worshipped idols only
Sinned
questions.e: Romans 3:23 states, 'For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God.' This verse establishes the universal need for justification through Christ, since no one is sinless.
questions.p: Romans 3:23 talk say everybody don sin, and dem no reach the glory of God. Na why everybody need Christ make dem fit stand well before God.

questions.q: In Galatians 2:16, Paul argues that a person is justified before God not by works of the law but through what?
o: Offering animal sacrifices
Faith in Jesus Christ
Observing Jewish festivals
Good deeds alone
questions.e: Galatians 2:16 says a person 'is not justified by the works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ.' Paul emphasises that trust in Christ, not legal observance, brings right standing with God; this is central to the law-versus-grace debate in the Epistles.
questions.p: Galatians 2:16 talk say person no dey justify through law work, na through faith for Jesus Christ. Paul dey show say na trust for Christ dey bring better relationship with God, no be say you follow law well-well.

questions.q: In Romans 12:6-8, Paul lists gifts that differ according to the grace given to each believer. According to this passage, how should a person with the gift of giving exercise it?
o: With bold leadership only
With cheerful mercy to strangers
With liberality and simplicity
With teaching and knowledge
questions.e: Romans 12:8 instructs that the one who gives should do so 'with liberality' (simplicity, generosity). Paul matches each gift with a fitting manner of exercising it, showing that gifts must be used appropriately and sincerely, not for show.
questions.p: Romans 12:8 talk say the one wey get gift of giving make e dey give with open heart, no be small-small or grudging. Paul show say each gift get the correct way wey person go use am well.

questions.q: According to John 1:17, through whom did grace and truth come, in contrast to the law which came through Moses?
o: Jesus Christ
Elijah
Abraham
Moses
questions.e: John 1:17 says, 'For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.' This verse highlights the New Testament contrast between the law under Moses and grace brought by Christ.
questions.p: John 1:17 talk say na through Moses the law come, but grace and truth come through Jesus Christ. Dis verse show the difference between law wey Moses bring and grace wey Christ bring.

questions.q: In Romans chapter 13, Paul teaches that Christians should submit to civil government. What reason does he give for this instruction?
o: Because civil law is more important than God's law
Because governing authorities have been established by God
Because believers should only obey leaders they personally like
Because the authorities are perfect and cannot make mistakes
questions.e: Paul says every soul should be subject to governing authorities because there is no authority except from God, and those that exist are appointed by Him. This teaches respect for lawful government as part of civic duty. See Romans 13:1-2.
questions.p: Paul talk say every person must dey obey government because na God put authority for der place. Dis one na about civic duty wey Christian suppose show. Na Romans 13:1-2.

questions.q: In Philippians chapter 2, Paul uses the example of Jesus Christ who humbled Himself and took the form of a servant. What virtue is Paul teaching the Philippian believers through this example?
o: Patience in suffering sickness
Courage in persecution
Wisdom in business dealings
Humility in relating with others
questions.e: Paul tells believers to have the same mind as Christ, who humbled Himself and became obedient even to death on the cross. This passage is a model of humility for Christian living. See Philippians 2:5-8.
questions.p: Paul tell believers make dem get mind like Jesus, wey humble Imself go die for cross. Na humility im dey teach as example for Christian living. Na Philippians 2:5-8.

questions.q: In 1 Thessalonians 5:2, Paul describes how the day of the Lord will come upon unprepared people. What image does he use to describe its sudden and unexpected arrival?
o: A shepherd searching for a lost sheep
A thief in the night
A farmer gathering his harvest
A fisherman casting his net
questions.e: Paul writes that the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, meaning it will arrive suddenly when people least expect it. This warns believers to stay watchful and ready for Christ's second coming. See 1 Thessalonians 5:2.
questions.p: Paul talk say the day of the Lord go come like how thief dey enter night time, nobody go sabi when e go reach. E dey warn believers make dem ready for Christ second coming. Na 1 Thessalonians 5:2.

questions.q: In Romans 12:1, Paul appeals to believers to present their bodies to God in a particular way as an act of reasonable worship. What does he call this offering?
o: A peace offering
A sin offering
A living sacrifice
A burnt offering
questions.e: Paul urges believers to present their bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which he calls their reasonable service. This teaches that true worship involves daily holy living, not just rituals. See Romans 12:1.
questions.p: Paul beg believers make dem give dia body as living sacrifice wey holy and dey please God, e call am reasonable service. E mean say real worship na how person dey live holy everyday. Na Romans 12:1.

questions.q: James, in his epistle, teaches about the relationship between faith and works. According to James 2:17, what is faith that has no accompanying works described as?
o: Faith that is strong
Faith that is growing
Faith that is perfect
Faith that is dead
questions.e: James teaches that faith without works is dead, meaning genuine faith must show itself through good deeds and righteous living. This is a key theme in the practical Christian living taught in his epistle. See James 2:17.
questions.p: James talk say faith wey no get work na dead faith, e mean say correct faith must show through good deeds and righteous life. Na im be practical Christian living wey James dey teach. Na James 2:17.

questions.q: In 2 Peter 3:10, Peter describes the day of the Lord coming unexpectedly like a thief, after which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise. What does he say will happen to the elements on that day?
o: They will melt with fervent heat
They will be rolled up like a scroll
They will turn into darkness
They will shine brighter than the sun
questions.e: Peter describes that on the day of the Lord, the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat, showing the dramatic and total transformation that will accompany Christ's second coming. See 2 Peter 3:10.
questions.p: Peter talk say on the day of the Lord, heaven go pass away with loud noise and the elements go melt because of strong heat. Dis one dey show the kain serious change wey go happen when Christ come back. Na 2 Peter 3:10.

questions.q: In 1 Timothy 2:1-2, Paul instructs Timothy that prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving should be made for kings and all in authority. What reason does Paul give for making such prayers?
o: So that believers may lead a peaceful and quiet life in godliness
So that kings will give money to the church
So that the church can gain political power
So that unbelievers will be punished by God
questions.e: Paul instructs that prayers be made for kings and all in authority so that believers may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. This shows that civic responsibility includes praying for leaders for the good of society. See 1 Timothy 2:1-2.
questions.p: Paul talk say make dem dey pray for kings and leaders so dat believers go fit live quiet and peaceful life wey get godliness. Dis one show say civic duty include to dey pray for leaders for society good. Na 1 Timothy 2:1-2.

questions.q: According to Hebrews 13:17, believers are told to obey those who rule over them in the church because such leaders watch for their souls as those who must give what to God?
o: Reports to the civil government
Sacrifices on their behalf
Tithes and offerings
An account for the souls under their care
questions.e: Hebrews 13:17 teaches that church leaders watch over the souls of believers because they will give an account to God for how they led them. Believers are therefore urged to obey and submit to such leaders joyfully. See Hebrews 13:17.
questions.p: Hebrews 13:17 teach say church leaders dey watch over believers soul because dem go give account to God for how dem lead dem. Na im make believers suppose dey obey dia leaders well well. Na Hebrews 13:17.

questions.q: According to Genesis chapter one, what did God declare after completing all the works of creation and looking at everything He had made?
o: That it needed further improvement
That it was finished forever
That it was very good
That man should perfect it
questions.e: Genesis 1:31 says God saw everything He had made and it was very good. This shows His satisfaction with a perfect creation.
questions.p: Genesis 1:31 tok say as God finish to create everything, e look am and see say e good well well. Dis one show say God dey happy with wetin e create.

questions.q: In Genesis chapter two, what was the specific consequence God warned Adam about if he ate from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil?
o: He would become like the beasts
He would be driven out of Eden immediately
He would surely die
He would lose his dominion over animals
questions.e: Genesis 2:17 records God's warning that in the day Adam ate of that tree, he would surely die. This was a direct command showing God's authority over His creation.
questions.p: Genesis 2:17 show us clear say God warn Adam make e no chop dat fruit, or else e must to die. Dis na to show say na God get final say over everything.

questions.q: On the sixth day of creation, after making land animals, what further unique act did God perform that marked the climax of His creative work?
o: He separated the waters above and below
He created the sun and moon
He blessed the seventh day
He formed man in His own image
questions.e: Genesis 1:26-27 shows that on the sixth day, after creating land animals, God made man in His own image, the high point of creation week.
questions.p: Genesis 1:26-27 make am plain say for the sixth day, after God make animal, naim e create man for e own image. Naim be the highest work wey God do.

questions.q: A student argues that Genesis chapter two contradicts chapter one because in chapter two, man appears to be formed before plants and animals. What is the best explanation for this arrangement?
o: Chapter two replaces the account in chapter one entirely
Chapter two gives a detailed, focused account of man's creation and his environment rather than a strict chronological order
Chapter two proves animals were never created
Chapter one was written by a different God
questions.e: Genesis chapter two zooms in on man's formation, his garden home and companion, giving detail rather than repeating the day-by-day sequence of chapter one. The two accounts complement rather than contradict each other.
questions.p: Genesis chapter two just come explain more about how God create man and put am for garden, e no mean say e dey fight chapter one. Dem both dey support each other to make sense.

questions.q: According to Genesis chapter two, what task did God give Adam concerning the Garden of Eden before the woman was created?
o: To build an altar for worship
To gather food for the animals
To name all the stars
To dress and keep the garden
questions.e: Genesis 2:15 states that God put Adam in the garden to dress it and to keep it. This shows man's responsibility as a steward over God's creation.
questions.p: Genesis 2:15 tok say God carry Adam put for garden make e dey work am and clean am. Dis show say man get work to do as manager of God property.

questions.q: A teacher tells her class that the creation of the Sabbath in Genesis chapter two teaches a lesson about work and rest for humanity. Which verse best supports this teaching?
o: Genesis 1:11, where God commanded the earth to bring forth vegetation
Genesis 1:5, where God named the light Day
Genesis 2:2-3, where God rested on the seventh day and blessed it
Genesis 2:17, where God warned against eating the forbidden fruit
questions.e: Genesis 2:2-3 records that God rested on the seventh day, blessed it, and sanctified it, setting a pattern of rest after labour for humanity to follow.
questions.p: Genesis 2:2-3 explain say God rest for the seventh day and make am holy, so man too suppose dey rest after work.

questions.q: In Genesis chapter one, God gave man dominion over the fish of the sea, birds of the air, and every living creature. What does this dominion primarily signify about man's place in creation?
o: Man was created only to worship the animals
Man was given delegated authority to responsibly rule over other creatures
Man has no accountability for how he treats animals
Man is equal to God in authority
questions.e: Genesis 1:28 shows God giving man dominion, meaning delegated authority under God to manage and care for creation responsibly, not unlimited or independent power.
questions.p: Genesis 1:28 show say God give man power to command other creatures, meaning say na God give us authority make we take care of the world well.

questions.q: In Genesis 3, after Adam and Eve disobeyed God, what was the immediate emotional response that caused them to hide themselves among the trees of the garden?
o: Fear and shame
Jealousy of each other
Hunger for more fruit
Anger at the serpent
questions.e: Adam told God he was afraid because he was naked, and he hid himself. This shows that fear and shame were the immediate results of disobedience.
questions.p: Adam tell God say im fear because im naked, and im hide. Dis show say fear and shame na di immediate result of disobedience.

questions.q: When God questioned Adam about eating the forbidden fruit, Adam's response revealed a key consequence of sin in human relationships. What did Adam do in his reply to God?
o: He pleaded for immediate forgiveness
He accused the serpent directly
He blamed the woman and indirectly God Himself
He confessed his sin openly without excuse
questions.e: Adam said the woman God gave him made him eat the fruit, shifting blame to Eve and hinting that God was responsible for giving her to him. This shows how sin brought blame-shifting and broken relationships.
questions.p: Adam talk say di woman wey God give am make am chop di fruit, im con shift blame give Eve and even hint say God cause am. Dis show how sin bring blame-shifting and broken relationship.

questions.q: In Genesis 4, what did God tell Cain would happen to sin if he did not master it, shortly before he killed Abel?
o: Sin would pass to his descendants only
Sin lay at the door and desired to have him, but he should rule over it
Sin would be forgiven automatically
Sin would destroy his offering permanently
questions.e: God warned Cain that sin crouched at the door desiring to control him, but he was commanded to master it. This warning came before Cain allowed jealousy to lead him into murder.
questions.p: God warn Cain say sin dey wait for door like person wey wan control am, but im suppose rule over am. Dis warning happen before Cain allow jealousy make am commit murder.

questions.q: After God rejected Cain's offering but accepted Abel's, what does this incident primarily teach about acceptable worship in the Genesis account?
o: Only animal sacrifices please God
Firstborn sons must always offer sacrifices
God never rejects any sincere offering
The attitude and manner of the offerer matter to God, not just the type of gift
questions.e: Hebrews later explains that Abel offered by faith, showing that the heart and manner behind an offering matter, not merely its physical form. Cain's offering was rejected because of his attitude, as shown by his anger and subsequent sin.
questions.p: Hebrews explain later say Abel offer by faith, wey show say di heart and manner of worship matter pass ordinary physical gift. God reject Cain offering because of im bad attitude.

questions.q: As part of Cain's punishment after murdering Abel, what specific lifestyle did God pronounce upon him regarding the ground and his dwelling?
o: He would be struck blind immediately
He would become a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth
He would be killed by his own children
He would lose the ability to speak
questions.e: God told Cain that the ground would no longer yield its strength to him and that he would be a restless wanderer on the earth. This was the direct consequence of his brother's blood crying out from the ground.
questions.p: God tell Cain say ground no go produce for am again and say im go be fugitive and wanderer for earth. Na dis punishment follow di blood of im brother wey cry from ground.

questions.q: Before the flood, the Bible records that God observed the wickedness of man had become great on the earth. Which description best captures God's own assessment of humanity's condition that led Him to decide to destroy all living creatures?
o: Humans had begun worshipping idols made of gold
People had abandoned farming for hunting
Every imagination of man's heart was only evil continually
Mankind had simply stopped offering sacrifices
questions.e: Genesis records that God saw the wickedness of man was great, and every imagination of his heart's thoughts was only evil continually. This deep corruption grieved God and led to His decision to send the flood.
questions.p: Genesis record say God see say wickedness of man don too much, and every imagination of im heart na only evil all di time. Dis deep corruption make God grieve and decide to send flood.

questions.q: Considering the overall narrative from the fall of man through Babel, which statement best summarises a common pattern seen in God's dealings with human sin in these accounts?
o: God always destroys sinners instantly without warning
God only punishes sin committed by leaders, not ordinary people
God ignores sin once it has been committed
God judges sin but also shows mercy or provides a way forward for mankind
questions.e: In each account, from clothing Adam and Eve, sparing Cain's life with a mark, saving Noah's family in the ark, to scattering rather than destroying the builders at Babel, God judged sin but also showed mercy. This pattern reveals God's justice balanced with grace throughout these narratives.
questions.p: For all di story, from Adam and Eve, Cain, Noah, reach Babel, God dey judge sin but im still dey show mercy. Dis pattern show say God justice and grace dey go together.

questions.q: After the flood, God instructed Noah and his sons concerning the eating of meat. According to Genesis 9, what was Noah forbidden to eat?
o: Meat with the blood still in it
Meat offered to idols
Meat of animals that chew the cud
Meat of birds of the air
questions.e: Genesis 9:4 forbids eating flesh with its life, that is its blood, still in it. This was part of the instructions God gave Noah after the flood.
questions.p: God tell Noah for Genesis 9:4 say make dem no chop meat wey blood still dey inside because life dey the blood. Na part of the direct instruction wey God give Noah after the flood.

questions.q: In Genesis 17, God changed Abram's name to Abraham as part of the covenant. What is the meaning of the new name 'Abraham'?
o: God is my strength
Father of faith
Father of many nations
Friend of God
questions.e: Genesis 17:5 explains that Abram became Abraham because God had made him a father of many nations. The name change showed the covenant promise of numerous descendants.
questions.p: For Genesis 17:5, God change Abram name to Abraham because He don make am father of many nations. The name change show the covenant promise say im descendants go plenty.
