questions.q: Before Israel received the Ten Commandments at Sinai, God described what special status the nation would have among all peoples if they kept His covenant. What was this status called?
o: A people greater than Egypt
A peculiar treasure and a kingdom of priests
A royal army of conquest
A nation of judges and prophets
questions.e: Exodus 19:5-6 states that Israel would be a peculiar treasure unto God above all people and a kingdom of priests, a holy nation, if they obeyed His voice and kept His covenant.
questions.p: Exodus 19:5-6 tok say if Israel go obey God voice and keep His covenant, dem go be like special treasure and kingdom of priests to God.

questions.q: God made a covenant with Noah that included every living creature on earth, not just human beings. Which of these best shows the wide scope of this covenant as recorded in Genesis 9?
o: The covenant was limited to Noah's three sons alone
The covenant applied only to clean animals used for sacrifice
The covenant excluded fish and creatures of the sea
The covenant included the birds, cattle and every beast of the earth
questions.e: Genesis 9:9-10 shows God establishing His covenant with Noah, his descendants, and every living creature that came out of the ark, including birds and cattle. This makes the covenant universal in scope, unlike the later covenants with Abraham and Israel which focused on a chosen people.
questions.p: Genesis 9:9-10 show say God covenant with Noah reach everybody, including birds, cattle, and all the beast dem wey waka commot from the ark.

questions.q: When God confirmed His covenant with Abraham in Genesis 15, He asked Abraham to bring certain animals which were divided, with a smoking furnace and burning lamp passing between the pieces. What did this ceremony signify?
o: God alone was solemnly binding Himself to fulfil the covenant promise
Abraham was being tested for obedience like Job
The animals represented the nations Abraham would conquer
Abraham was offering a sacrifice for his sins
questions.e: In Genesis 15:17-18, only the smoking furnace and burning lamp, representing God's presence, passed between the divided animals while Abraham was in a deep sleep. This ancient covenant ritual showed that God alone took the oath to fulfil His promise.
questions.p: For Genesis 15:17-18, na only the smoking furnace and burning lamp pass through the meat while Abraham dey sleep. This one show say na God alone swear to fulfill the covenant promise.

questions.q: At Mount Sinai, the Israelites were commanded to prepare themselves for three days before God spoke to them. Which of the following was part of this preparation according to Exodus 19?
o: They offered burnt offerings of bulls for three days
They fasted completely from food and water
They washed their clothes and were told not to touch the mountain
They built an altar of stones at the foot of the mountain
questions.e: Exodus 19:10-12 records that the people were to wash their clothes and sanctify themselves, and bounds were set around the mountain so no one would touch it. This showed the holiness required before meeting with God.
questions.p: Exodus 19:10-12 tok say make the people wash dia clothes and make dem no touch the mountain. This one show the holy life wey God want before He go meet dem.

questions.q: A Sunday school teacher in Enugu explains that God's covenant with Abraham was unconditional in its initial promise, while the covenant at Sinai required Israel's obedience for its blessings. Which statement best supports this distinction?
o: God promised Abraham descendants and land based on His own will, while Sinai's blessings depended on Israel keeping the law
Both covenants demanded sacrifice of a son before they could be sealed
Abraham's covenant required temple worship while Sinai's did not
Sinai's covenant came with land promises but Abraham's did not
questions.e: In Genesis 12 and 15, God freely promised Abraham land and descendants without conditions attached to the initial promise. In contrast, Exodus 19:5 makes Israel's covenant blessings dependent on obeying God's voice and keeping His covenant.
questions.p: God promise Abraham land and pikin base on His own grace, but Sinai covenant deyaka make Israel obey law before dem go get the blessing.

questions.q: According to Genesis 9, God set a specific sign in the sky as a reminder of His covenant with Noah and all living creatures. What natural phenomenon did God use as this sign?
o: A bright star
The rainbow
The full moon
The rising sun
questions.e: Genesis 9:13 records that God set His rainbow in the cloud as a token of the covenant between Him and the earth, promising never again to destroy all life with a flood.
questions.p: Genesis 9:13 explain say na rainbow God put for cloud as sign of the covenant say He no go use water destroy everywhere again.

questions.q: Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers in Egypt during their second visit for grain. What reason did Joseph give for not being angry with them for selling him into slavery?
o: He had already forgiven them before leaving Canaan
Their father Jacob had pleaded with him in a dream
The Egyptian priests advised him to forgive them
God sent him ahead to preserve life during the famine
questions.e: Joseph told his brothers that God had sent him ahead of them to preserve life, turning their evil intention into divine purpose. This shows God's providence working through human actions.
questions.p: Joseph tell im brothers say na God send am go before dem to save life, because wetin dem plan for evil, naam God use for good. E make us know say God dey direct wetin human beings dey do.

questions.q: At the burning bush on Mount Horeb, Moses raised an objection about his ability to lead Israel out of Egypt. What was this particular objection?
o: He was not eloquent and was slow of speech
He was too old for such a difficult task
He feared Pharaoh would have him killed immediately
He did not know the way to the promised land
questions.e: Moses told God he was not eloquent but slow of speech and slow of tongue, so God appointed Aaron to speak for him. This was one of several excuses Moses gave before accepting his call.
questions.p: Moses tell God say e no sabi talk well and im tongue heavy, naim make God give am Aaron make e dey talk for am. Na one of the reasons Moses give before e finally accept to do the work.

questions.q: Before his death, Moses commissioned a successor by the laying on of hands in the presence of Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. Who received this commission?
o: Phinehas
Aaron
Caleb
Joshua
questions.e: Moses laid his hands on Joshua son of Nun and commissioned him as leader of Israel, as instructed by God. Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom and the people obeyed him.
questions.p: Moses put im hand for Joshua head make am leader of Israel as God talk, con make Eleazar the priest and everybody witness am. Joshua get the spirit of wisdom and the people come dey obey am.

questions.q: After the Israelites crossed the Jordan River into Canaan, Joshua set up twelve stones taken from the riverbed. What was the main purpose of this memorial?
o: To honour the twelve spies sent earlier by Moses
To mark the boundary between the twelve tribes
To remind future generations how God dried up the Jordan
To serve as an altar for sacrifices to God
questions.e: Joshua set up the twelve stones so that when children asked about them in future, their fathers would explain how God dried up the Jordan for Israel to cross. It was a lasting memorial of God's mighty act.
questions.p: Joshua put those twelve stones so that when pikin dem ask for future, their papa go tell dem how God dry Jordan water make Israel pass. E be like monument to remember wetin God do.

questions.q: Gideon asked God for a sign using a fleece of wool before he agreed to lead Israel against the Midianites. What exactly did Gideon ask to happen to the fleece the first time?
o: The fleece should turn white as proof of God's favour
The fleece should be wet with dew while the ground around it stayed dry
The fleece should remain completely dry while the ground around it was wet with dew
The fleece should catch fire without being burnt up
questions.e: Gideon first asked that dew be only on the fleece while the ground remained dry, and God did exactly that. He later reversed the test for confirmation, asking for a dry fleece with dew on the ground.
questions.p: Gideon tell God make water (dew) only dey for the fleece of wool while ground dry, and God do am like that. Later, e still test God again say make the fleece dry and ground wet.

questions.q: Deborah summoned Barak and instructed him to gather an army against Sisera, but Barak insisted Deborah accompany him to battle. What did Deborah say would be the consequence of this condition?
o: Barak would lose the battle completely
The Lord would deliver Sisera into the hand of a woman
Israel would remain under Canaanite oppression longer
Barak would be replaced as commander by Gideon
questions.e: Deborah told Barak that because of his condition, the honour of the victory would go to a woman, not to him. This was fulfilled when Jael killed Sisera by driving a tent peg through his head.
questions.p: Deborah tell Barak say because say e want make she follow am go war, na woman hand God go take sell Sisera. Na so Jael come kill Sisera with tent peg for im head later.

questions.q: When the Israelites arrived at Rephidim, there was no water for the people to drink and they murmured against Moses. What did God instruct Moses to do at that place to provide water for the people?
o: Strike the rock at Horeb with his rod
Send spies to find a hidden spring
Pray over a dry riverbed until it filled with water
Dip a piece of cloth into a nearby well
questions.e: At Rephidim, God told Moses to strike the rock at Horeb with his rod, and water gushed out for the people to drink. This showed God's continued provision despite the people's complaining.
questions.p: For Rephidim, God tell Moses make e strike the rock for Horeb with im rod, and water come out for people to drink. This show say God dey provide for dem even when dem dey complain.

questions.q: Before the Israelites reached Mount Sinai, God tested their obedience through the way He provided food. Which instruction concerning the manna was meant to test whether the people would obey God's law?
o: They must cook the manna before eating it
They must share the manna equally with the Egyptians who followed them
They must not go out of the camp to gather manna on the Sabbath
They must store enough manna to last a full year
questions.e: God commanded that no manna would fall on the Sabbath, and the people were told to gather double the day before and rest on the seventh day. This instruction tested their obedience to God's law of rest.
questions.p: God command say no manna go fall for Sabbath day, and make dem gather double the day before. Dis instruction test weda dem go obey God law of rest.

questions.q: As the Israelites journeyed through the wilderness, God's providence was shown not only in feeding them but also in preserving their basic needs over many years. Which of the following is specifically recorded as a sign of God's sustaining care throughout the forty years in the wilderness?
o: They received silver and gold daily from heaven
Their cattle multiplied greatly every year
They never experienced any form of sickness
Their clothes and sandals did not wear out
questions.e: Moses reminded the people that throughout their forty years of wandering, their clothes did not wear out nor did their feet swell, showing God's continuous care and protection over them.
questions.p: Moses remind everybody say throughout their forty years for wilderness, dia clothes no tear and dia legs no swell. Dis show how God dey care and protect dem.

questions.q: A Sunday School teacher explains that God's guidance of Israel through the wilderness was not limited to physical direction but also included moral instruction for right living. Which event best illustrates God providing the Israelites with moral and religious guidance during the wilderness journey?
o: The sweetening of the water at Marah
The giving of the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai
The crossing of the Red Sea
The victory over the Amalekites
questions.e: At Mount Sinai, God gave Moses the Ten Commandments to guide the moral and religious conduct of the Israelites. This was God's way of providing them with a standard for right living, beyond mere physical direction.
questions.p: For Mount Sinai, God give Moses Ten Commandments to direct how the Israelites suppose dey live dia life. Na so God give dem standard for good behaviour and worship.

questions.q: Soon after leaving Egypt, the Israelites complained of hunger and longed for the food they used to eat in Egypt. Comparing God's response at this point with His response to their later complaint about lack of water at Rephidim, what common lesson do both incidents teach about divine providence?
o: God continues to provide for His people's needs even when they complain, showing His patience and faithfulness
God withdraws His blessings whenever the people disobey Him
God only helps those who have never complained against Him
God always punishes complaints with plagues before providing help
questions.e: Despite the people's repeated grumbling about hunger and thirst, God still provided manna and water for them instead of abandoning them. Both incidents together teach that God remains patient and faithful in meeting His people's needs even amid their weak faith.
questions.p: Even though the people dey grumble up and down for food and water, God still provide manna and water give dem. Both story teach us say God dey patient and faithful to supply wetin hin people need.

questions.q: During the journey, the Israelites were led to travel by a longer route through the wilderness rather than the shorter way through the land of the Philistines. What was God's main reason for choosing this longer route for His people?
o: To give Moses more time to receive the law
Because the Philistines had closed their borders
So that they would not be discouraged by the sight of war and return to Egypt
To test their skill in desert survival
questions.e: The Bible records that God led the people by the wilderness route because the shorter way through Philistine territory might expose them to war, which could discourage them and make them want to go back to Egypt. This shows God's protective guidance in planning their path.
questions.p: Bible tell us say God carry dem pass wilderness road because if dem face war for Philistine land, fear fit make dem turn back go Egypt. Dis show say God dey protect dia steps.

questions.q: Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, visited the Israelites in the wilderness and observed Moses judging the people's disputes alone from morning till evening. What advice did Jethro give Moses that became an important lesson in delegation and administration?
o: Moses should return all disputes to Pharaoh's officials who had handled such cases in Egypt
Moses should call a general assembly of the people to vote on every dispute brought to him
Moses should abandon the practice of judging disputes entirely and let the elders decide alone
Moses should appoint capable men to judge small matters while he handled only the difficult cases
questions.e: Jethro advised Moses to select able, God-fearing men to serve as judges over smaller matters, reserving only the hardest cases for himself. This relieved Moses of an unbearable burden and taught the value of delegating responsibility.
questions.p: Jethro tell Moses make e choose men wey fear God to help am judge small-small matter. Na so Moses take reduce im work and learn how to share responsibility.

questions.q: At Mount Sinai, before giving the Ten Commandments, God instructed Moses to prepare the people through a process of consecration. Which of the following was part of this preparation commanded by God?
o: The people were to build an altar of gold at the foot of the mountain
The people were to shave their heads as a sign of mourning before the covenant
The people were to fast completely from food and water for seven days
The people were to wash their clothes and abstain from sexual relations for a set period
questions.e: God told Moses to sanctify the people by having them wash their garments and remain pure, preparing them to meet Him on the third day. This showed that approaching God's presence required holiness and readiness.
questions.p: God tell Moses make the people wash their cloth and stay holy before dem meet am. This one show say person must dey clean before e fit stand for God presence.

questions.q: While Moses was on Mount Sinai receiving instructions from God, the Israelites below grew impatient and persuaded Aaron to make them a god they could see. What object did Aaron fashion for the people, and what consequence followed when Moses came down?
o: Aaron made a silver lamp, and Moses immediately crowned a new leader in his place
Aaron made a golden calf, and Moses broke the tablets of the law in anger before dealing with the people
Aaron made a wooden ark, and Moses ordered the people to carry it round the camp seven times
Aaron made a bronze serpent, and Moses commanded that it be kept in the tabernacle
questions.e: Aaron cast a golden calf from the people's earrings, and when Moses saw the idolatry, he broke the tablets written by God before confronting the people. This event shows how quickly the people turned from God despite His recent deliverance.
questions.p: Aaron make golden calf for the people, and when Moses see wetin dem do, e break the stone tablets. This show say the people quick forget God after all the good things wey E do for dem.

questions.q: God instructed Moses to build a portable sanctuary so that He might dwell among the Israelites during their wilderness journey. What was this sanctuary called, and what was its main purpose?
o: The synagogue, a permanent stone building for teaching the law to children
The temple, a fixed structure built later by Solomon for national worship
The tabernacle, a movable tent where God's presence met with Israel and sacrifices were offered
The citadel, a fortress built to protect the Israelites from Amalekite attacks
questions.e: The tabernacle was a portable tent of meeting constructed according to God's pattern, serving as the dwelling place of His presence among the people as they travelled. It also housed the ark and was the centre for offering sacrifices.
questions.p: The tabernacle na the tent wey God tell Moses make e build so that He go fit stay with the people. Na there dem dey keep the ark and offer sacrifice to God.

questions.q: Immediately after crossing the Red Sea in safety while the Egyptian army was drowned, Moses and the Israelites responded to God's deliverance. What did they do to express their gratitude for this protection?
o: Moses and the people sang a song of praise to God, and Miriam led the women in dance with timbrels
The people demanded that Aaron be made king over them as a reward for the victory
Moses ordered the immediate construction of a golden altar in thanksgiving before moving on
Moses sent a delegation back to Pharaoh to negotiate peace between the two nations
questions.e: After witnessing God's deliverance at the Red Sea, Moses and the Israelites broke into a song celebrating God's victory, and Miriam the prophetess led the women in dancing with timbrels. This was a direct, joyful response of worship to divine protection.
questions.p: After God save them for Red Sea, Moses and the people sing song of praise. Miriam come lead the women make dem dance with timbrel to thank God.

questions.q: A Sunday school teacher compares two instances of Israel lacking water in the wilderness, at Rephidim early in the journey and at Kadesh much later, to teach a lesson on obedience. What was the key difference in God's instruction to Moses on how to bring forth water on these two separate occasions?
o: At Rephidim Moses was told to strike the rock, but at Kadesh he was told only to speak to the rock
At Rephidim Moses was told to speak to the rock, but at Kadesh he was told to strike it twice
Both times Moses was told to strike the rock in exactly the same way without any difference
At Rephidim the people were given water from a well dug by the elders, not from a rock at all
questions.e: At Rephidim God told Moses to strike the rock with his rod, but years later at Kadesh God commanded him only to speak to the rock. Moses disobeyed by striking it instead, which led to his being barred from entering the promised land.
questions.p: For Rephidim, God tell Moses make e strike the rock, but for Kadesh, e tell am make e just talk to the rock. Moses come strike the rock instead, and that one make God vex for am.

questions.q: While encamped near the Amalekites' territory, the Israelites faced an unexpected attack on their journey. Joshua was appointed to lead the fighting men into battle. What was the eventual outcome of this encounter, and how was it commemorated?
o: Israel fled from the battle entirely, and God sent fire to destroy the Amalekite camp instead
The two nations signed a peace treaty, and Moses erected twelve stones as witnesses
Israel was defeated by the Amalekites, and Moses fasted for forty days in mourning
Israel defeated the Amalekites, and Moses built an altar calling it 'The LORD is my banner'
questions.e: Joshua led Israel to victory over the Amalekites while Moses' raised hands, supported by Aaron and Hur, ensured success. In remembrance of God's help, Moses built an altar and named it Jehovah-nissi, meaning 'The LORD is my banner'.
questions.p: Joshua lead Israel win the Amalekites while Moses lift im hand up. To remember how God help them, Moses build altar and call am Jehovah-nissi, wey mean say God na our banner.

questions.q: Hannah made a vow to God at Shiloh concerning the son she desired. Which part of the vow specifically describes the kind of life Samuel would live?
o: He would never speak to his father
He would fast every day of his life
No razor would ever touch his head
He would never marry throughout his life
questions.e: Hannah vowed that if God gave her a son, no razor would touch his head, meaning Samuel would be a Nazirite dedicated to God. This marked him out for lifelong service.
questions.p: Hannah promise God sey if E give am pikin, no razor go touch im head. Dis one show sey Samuel na Nazirite wey dem dedicate for God service for im whole life.

questions.q: When the LORD called Samuel a fourth time, what instruction had Eli already given the boy to help him respond correctly?
o: To cover his ears and sleep again
To say, 'Speak, for thy servant heareth'
To wake Eli before answering
To run outside the tabernacle immediately
questions.e: Eli discerned that it was God calling Samuel and instructed him to respond, 'Speak, for thy servant heareth.' This showed Eli's spiritual guidance despite his earlier failures.
questions.p: Eli come sabi sey na God dey call Samuel, so E tell am wetin to talk. E tell Samuel make E say, 'Speak, for thy servant heareth' so dat God go fit talk to am.

questions.q: God's first message to young Samuel concerned judgement on Eli's household. What made this judgement particularly severe according to the message?
o: Eli himself committed the same sins as his sons
Eli's sons refused to serve at the tabernacle
Eli knew of his sons' sins but failed to restrain them
Eli did not know about his sons' sins at all
questions.e: God's message explained that Eli knew his sons were sinning against God yet did not restrain them, making him guilty of neglecting his parental duty. This failure to discipline brought severe judgement on his house.
questions.p: God tell Samuel sey Eli house go suffer because Eli know sey im pikin dem dey do bad, but E no stop dem. Eli fail im duty as papa, so God come judge am.

questions.q: Comparing Eli's parenting with Hannah's dedication of Samuel, what key lesson emerges for parents today?
o: Children should be left entirely to religious leaders to train
Only mothers bear responsibility for a child's moral training
Strictness in discipline is less important than material provision
Godly upbringing and discipline matter more than mere position or privilege
questions.e: Eli held a high priestly position but failed to discipline his sons, while Hannah's dedication produced a godly Samuel. The contrast teaches that sincere godly training, not status, shapes a child's character.
questions.p: Eli get high position but E no train im pikin dem well, while Hannah train Samuel for God way. Dis one teach us sey na godly training dey make pikin get better character, no be just position.

questions.q: As Samuel grew older, what evidence from his early life showed that God's hand of favour was upon him, in contrast to Eli's sons?
o: He grew in favour with the Lord and with men
He married early and had many children
He became wealthy through trade in Shiloh
He led armies against the Philistines as a youth
questions.e: The scripture records that Samuel grew in favour both with the LORD and with men, unlike Hophni and Phinehas who were corrupt. This showed the result of godly upbringing and personal devotion.
questions.p: Bible talk sey Samuel dey grow for favour for God and man eye. Dis one show sey Samuel life dey different from Eli pikin dem wey dey do bad.

questions.q: When Samuel eventually told Eli all that God had revealed to him about the coming judgement, how did Eli respond?
o: He asked Samuel to pray for his sons' forgiveness
He accepted it as the will of the Lord
He denied that his sons had sinned
He drove Samuel away from the tabernacle
questions.e: Despite the painful message, Eli humbly submitted, saying, 'It is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good.' This response showed his acceptance of divine judgement even though it came late to correct his earlier parental failure.
questions.p: Even as the message pain Eli, E still humble imsef and accept wetin God talk. E say make God do wetin E think say good, because E know sey na God talk am.

questions.q: At Jesse's house in Bethlehem, Samuel examined several of Jesse's older sons before David was identified as God's chosen one. What did this process teach about God's standard for choosing a leader?
o: God chooses whoever the father prefers most
God looks at the heart rather than outward appearance
God chooses based on birth order among brothers
God chooses based on a person's height and handsomeness
questions.e: God told Samuel not to judge by outward appearance or stature, for the LORD looks at the heart. This explains why David, the youngest and overlooked son, was chosen over his elder brothers.
questions.p: God tell Samuel make E no look person face or how tall the person be. God talk sey E dey look heart, no be wetin eye dey see, na why E choose David.

questions.q: Saul's jealousy of David grew after the women of Israel sang a song comparing their achievements in battle. What did the women sing that angered Saul?
o: Saul is our king, but David is our deliverer
Saul has built the temple, but David has built the kingdom
David has slain Goliath, and Saul has slain the Philistines
Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands
questions.e: The women's song praised David above Saul, saying Saul had slain thousands while David had slain ten thousands. This made Saul jealous and suspicious of David, leading to his disobedience and hatred.
questions.p: The women dem song praise David pass Saul, as dem yarn say Saul kill thousands but David kill ten thousands. This tin make Saul jealous and e begin suspect David, wey con make am disobey God and hate am.

questions.q: While fleeing from Saul, David had two clear opportunities to kill him but refused, even when his men urged him to do so. What reason did David give for sparing Saul's life on these occasions?
o: Saul was the Lord's anointed and David would not harm him
David believed Samuel would curse him if he killed Saul
David wanted Jonathan to inherit the throne peacefully
David feared Saul's army would avenge his death
questions.e: David respected Saul as God's anointed king, both in the cave at En-gedi and in Saul's camp. He left Saul's punishment to God rather than taking vengeance himself, showing obedience to God's order of authority.
questions.p: David respect Saul as God anointed king for inside cave and camp. E leave Saul punishment for God hand instead make e revenge, wey show say e dey obey God authority.

questions.q: Comparing Saul's reign with David's reign, which contrast best explains why David is regarded as a man after God's own heart despite his personal failures?
o: David consulted mediums for guidance, while Saul always obeyed Samuel
David never sinned against God, while Saul sinned repeatedly
David repented sincerely when confronted with his sins, while Saul often justified his disobedience
David rejected God's prophets, while Saul honoured them
questions.e: Although both kings sinned, David humbly accepted correction and repented, as seen after Nathan's rebuke, while Saul made excuses and blamed others. This difference in response to sin is why David remained favoured despite his faults.
questions.p: Even though both king sin, David accept correction with humility and repent well well after Nathan rebuke am, unlike Saul wey dey give excuse. Na dis attitude make God still favor David despite im fault.

questions.q: After being rejected as king, Saul became troubled by an evil spirit. Whose music brought him temporary relief and comfort?
o: David's harp playing
Jonathan's singing
Samuel's prophetic songs
The priests' temple music
questions.e: David was brought to Saul's court to play the harp whenever the evil spirit troubled him. His music soothed Saul and gave him temporary refreshment.
questions.p: Dem bring David come Saul palace make e dey play harp anytime evil spirit dey worry Saul. Im music dey sweet Saul body and give am relief.

questions.q: Jonathan's covenant of friendship with David is often cited as an example of loyalty that surpassed family loyalty to Saul. What specific action demonstrated the depth of this covenant?
o: Jonathan refused to become king after Saul's death
Jonathan handed over the kingdom to David while Saul was still alive
Jonathan warned David of Saul's plan to kill him and helped him escape
Jonathan fought against Saul's army to protect David
questions.e: Jonathan risked his father's anger to warn David of danger and helped him flee, proving his loyalty to their covenant friendship over his own interest in the throne. This act of sacrifice shows true friendship rooted in obedience to a higher moral duty.
questions.p: Jonathan risk im papa anger to warn David about danger and help am runot, wey prove say im loyalty to dia friendship pass crown. Dis sacrifice show true friendship based on God standard.

questions.q: David's disobedience in conducting a census of Israel and Judah brought punishment upon the nation. What form did this punishment take?
o: The loss of his throne to Absalom
A famine that lasted seven years
A defeat in battle against the Philistines
A severe pestilence that killed many people
questions.e: David's pride in numbering the people without relying on God angered the Lord, who sent a plague that killed many Israelites. David later repented and built an altar to stop the punishment.
questions.p: David pride to count people without God approval anger God, and God send heavy sickness wey kill plenty Israelites. Later David repent and build altar make punishment stop.

questions.q: A Sunday school teacher tells her class that Saul's disobedience in the war against the Amalekites was not a single random act but revealed a deeper character flaw that had shown earlier when he unlawfully offered a burnt sacrifice before a battle. What common weakness links both incidents?
o: Fear of Samuel's prophetic authority
Impatience and a desire to please the people rather than fully obey God
Excessive generosity towards defeated enemies
Strong loyalty to his family above God's commands
questions.e: In both the sacrifice at Gilgal and the sparing of Amalekite plunder, Saul acted out of impatience and fear of losing the people's support, rather than trusting and fully obeying God's instructions. This recurring weakness ultimately cost him the kingdom.
questions.p: For Gilgal sacrifice and Amalekite matter, Saul show impatience and fear of man instead make e obey God fully. Na dis constant weakness make am lose im kingship.

questions.q: Before he became king, David served in Saul's palace in two main capacities. What were they?
o: A harpist and an armour-bearer
A priest and a judge
A scribe and a tax collector
A shepherd and a prophet
questions.e: David played the harp to soothe Saul's troubled spirit and later became his armour-bearer. This drew him close to the royal household before he became king.
questions.p: Na David play harp to cool Saul spirit before e come later turn im armour-bearer. Dis one make am come near royal house before e come later become king.

questions.q: After Nathan confronted David over his sin, David composed a prayer of repentance that is preserved in the Book of Psalms. Which Psalm is traditionally linked with David's confession and plea for a clean heart?
o: Psalm 1
Psalm 23
Psalm 51
Psalm 121
questions.e: Psalm 51 is David's penitential prayer asking God to create in him a clean heart after his sin with Bathsheba was exposed. It shows his genuine sorrow and desire for restoration.
questions.p: Psalm 51 na David prayer wey e take beg God make e create clean heart for am after wey im sin with Bathsheba open. E show say e really sorry and want make God clean am.

questions.q: King David wanted to build a permanent house for the Ark of the Covenant, but God, through the prophet Nathan, gave him a different instruction. What did God tell David?
o: David himself would never see Jerusalem again
David should first conquer all surrounding nations
David must first rebuild the altar at Shiloh
David's son, not David, would build the temple
questions.e: God told David through Nathan that because he was a man of war, his son Solomon would be the one to build the temple. David instead made extensive preparations for it.
questions.p: God tell David through Nathan say because na man of war e be, na im pikin Solomon go build temple. But David still prepare plenty material for the work.

questions.q: Which event marked the climax of Solomon's temple-building achievement, showing that God accepted the new house of worship in Jerusalem?
o: Solomon relocated the temple to Shechem
The glory of the Lord filled the temple at its dedication
The Ark of the Covenant was destroyed by fire
Solomon offered his own son as a sacrifice
questions.e: At the dedication of the temple, the cloud of God's glory filled the house so that the priests could not continue ministering. This showed divine approval of Solomon's completed work.
questions.p: When dem dey dedicate temple, cloud of God glory full inside house reach extent wey priest dem no fit stand minister. Dis one show say God accept wetin Solomon do.

questions.q: One major cause of Solomon's spiritual downfall, as recorded in Scripture, was his unlawful political alliances. What practice led him into idolatry?
o: Marrying many foreign wives who turned his heart to other gods
Appointing foreigners as high priests
Refusing to pay tribute to neighbouring kings
Abolishing the temple sacrifices
questions.e: Solomon married many foreign women for political alliances, and in his old age they turned his heart to worship other gods. This disobedience provoked God's judgment on his kingdom.
questions.p: Solomon marry plenty foreign wives for political reasons, and as e old, dem turn im heart make e start to dey worship other gods. Dis disobedience make God vex for im kingdom.

questions.q: During David's reign, a man named Uriah suffered the direct consequence of the king's sin. What was Uriah's role before David's wrongdoing against him?
o: He was a prophet in Jerusalem
He was the high priest of Israel
He was a Hittite soldier in David's army
He was David's court musician
questions.e: Uriah the Hittite was a loyal soldier fighting in David's army when David committed adultery with his wife Bathsheba. David later arranged for Uriah to die in battle to cover his sin.
questions.p: Uriah the Hittite na loyal soldier for David army when David do bad thing with im wife Bathsheba. Later, David arrange make dem kill Uriah for battle to cover wetin e do.

questions.q: A queen from a distant land visited Solomon after hearing of his great wisdom and wealth. What was the main purpose of her visit, according to Scripture?
o: To request Solomon's help in building her own temple
To form a military alliance against Egypt
To demand tribute from Israel
To test Solomon with hard questions and see his wisdom for herself
questions.e: The Queen of Sheba came to test Solomon with difficult questions after hearing reports of his wisdom. She was amazed and confessed that the reports had not told her even half of it.
questions.p: Queen of Sheba come test Solomon with hard questions after she hear about im wisdom. When she reach, she shock and talk say wetin she hear no be half of wetin she eyes see.

questions.q: A student argues that David's reign had no lasting negative consequences because he repented of his sin with Bathsheba. Which later event in David's family life best shows this claim is mistaken?
o: David's victory song after defeating Goliath
The rebellion and strife that arose among David's own sons
The famine that struck Israel for three years
David's defeat of the Ammonites
questions.e: Despite David's genuine repentance, Nathan warned that trouble would never depart from his household, and this was fulfilled through conflict and rebellion among his sons, such as Absalom. This shows that forgiveness did not erase all earthly consequences of his sin.
questions.p: Even though God forgive David, Nathan bin warn am say wahala no go commot for im house. Dis one happen true true through fight and rebellion among im pikin dem like Absalom.

questions.q: Which prophet originally told Jeroboam that he would be given rule over ten tribes of Israel, tearing a new garment into twelve pieces to illustrate the message?
o: Iddo the seer
Shemaiah the prophet
Nathan the prophet
Ahijah the Shilonite
questions.e: Ahijah met Jeroboam on the road and tore his garment into twelve pieces, giving him ten to show he would rule ten tribes. This fulfilled God's judgement on Solomon's house for idolatry.
questions.p: Na Ahijah meet Jeroboam for road come tear im cloth into twelve pieces. E give Jeroboam ten pieces to show say God don choose am to rule ten tribes of Israel.

questions.q: Why did King Solomon seek to kill Jeroboam before Solomon's death, forcing Jeroboam to flee to Egypt?
o: Jeroboam had led a tax revolt in Jerusalem
Jeroboam had married a foreign princess against Solomon's wish
Jeroboam had been told he would become king over part of Israel
Jeroboam had refused to pay tribute to Solomon
questions.e: After Ahijah's prophecy became known, Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam to protect his throne, so Jeroboam escaped to Egypt until Solomon died. He only returned when Israel called him to challenge Rehoboam.
questions.p: When Solomon hear say Jeroboam go be king, e wan kill am. Jeroboam come run go Egypt hide until Solomon die.

questions.q: What was the main reason the elders advised Rehoboam to speak kindly and lighten the people's burden?
o: To prevent Egypt from attacking Judah
To win the people's loyal service forever
To secure more tribute from foreign nations
To please the prophet Ahijah
questions.e: The old men who had served Solomon advised Rehoboam that if he spoke kindly to the people and served them, they would be his servants forever. He rejected this wise counsel for the harsh advice of the younger men.
questions.p: The old men tell Rehoboam say if e treat the people well, dem go serve am forever. But Rehoboam no listen to dem wise talk.

questions.q: What immediate consequence followed when Rehoboam announced he would make the people's yoke heavier than his father's?
o: The ten northern tribes rebelled and rejected the house of David
The elders resigned from his council in protest
The people immediately crowned him king over all Israel
Judah and Israel went to war the same day
questions.e: On hearing Rehoboam's harsh response, the people of Israel cried out that they had no portion in David, and the ten tribes withdrew their allegiance. This led directly to the division of the kingdom.
questions.p: When the people hear say Rehoboam go make their work harder, dem reject am. The ten tribes come comot from the house of David immediately.

questions.q: Jeroboam feared that if the people continued going to Jerusalem to worship, their hearts would turn back to Rehoboam. What underlying lesson about leadership does this reveal?
o: True worship always strengthens political unity
Insecurity can lead a leader to introduce false worship to protect his power
Jeroboam genuinely desired to reform Israelite worship
Jerusalem's temple was no longer a valid place of worship
questions.e: Jeroboam's fear of losing political control, not religious conviction, drove him to set up alternative shrines at Bethel and Dan. This shows how personal insecurity can corrupt a leader's judgement and lead a nation into sin.
questions.p: Jeroboam fear say if the people go Jerusalem, dem go leave am. So e create fake worship for Bethel and Dan just to keep im power.

questions.q: Besides setting up golden calves, what other religious change did Jeroboam make that further departed from the law of Moses?
o: He introduced circumcision on the eighth day only
He built a new temple larger than Solomon's
He appointed priests who were not from the tribe of Levi
He abolished the Sabbath observance completely
questions.e: Jeroboam appointed priests from among all the people instead of restricting the priesthood to the Levites as the law required. This was part of his broader scheme to create an independent religious system separate from Jerusalem.
questions.p: Jeroboam pick priests from any tribe instead of the Levites wey God choose. E do this one to make sure say im own religion different from the one for Jerusalem.

questions.q: What theological lesson is best illustrated by the split of Solomon's kingdom into Judah and Israel under Rehoboam and Jeroboam?
o: Disobedience to God's commands can bring lasting national consequences
Military strength always determines who becomes king
Foreign alliances guarantee a stable kingdom
Wealth automatically secures a leader's popularity
questions.e: The division was a direct consequence of Solomon's idolatry and Rehoboam's foolish harshness, showing that disobedience brings serious national judgement. The kingdom never reunited, demonstrating the lasting effect of such failures.
questions.p: The way the kingdom divide show say disobedience to God get serious consequence. Solomon and Rehoboam actions cause problem wey no ever end.

questions.q: How did Jeroboam change the timing of the religious feast that was normally kept in the seventh month, moving it to the eighth month instead?
o: He shifted it to align with the Egyptian calendar
He cancelled the feast entirely for all Israel
He moved it to honour a victory over Judah
He devised it in his own heart to keep Israel from going to Jerusalem
questions.e: Jeroboam invented a feast in the eighth month, similar to the one in Judah, purely from his own heart to keep the northern tribes from travelling to Jerusalem to worship. This was another step in establishing rival worship centres.
questions.p: Jeroboam just create im own feast for the eighth month from im own head. E do am so that the people no go get reason to travel go Jerusalem for worship.

questions.q: After the contest on Mount Carmel, Elijah prayed earnestly and sent his servant seven times to look toward the sea before rain finally came, ending the long drought. What important lesson about prayer does this event teach?
o: Persistence and faith in prayer bring results even when answers are delayed
Prayer is unnecessary once a miracle has already been performed
Servants must always confirm a prophet's prayers before they are valid
God answers prayer only when offered on a mountain
questions.e: Elijah kept praying and sent his servant repeatedly until the small cloud appeared, showing that believers must persist in faith even when the answer seems delayed. This teaches patience and trust in God's timing.
questions.p: Elijah no give up, im con send im servant make im go look weather clouds don show. Dis dey teach us say make we dey patient and get faith for God even when our prayer answer delay.

questions.q: When Elijah complained to God at Horeb that he alone was left as a faithful worshipper and his enemies sought his life, how did God respond to correct his despair?
o: God rebuked him publicly before the people of Israel
God revealed Himself in a still small voice and told him seven thousand had not bowed to Baal
God commanded him to remain in the cave permanently
God told him to return immediately and fight Ahab's army
questions.e: At Horeb, God did not appear in the wind, earthquake, or fire but in a still small voice, assuring Elijah that seven thousand faithful Israelites remained who had not worshipped Baal. This encouraged Elijah that he was not alone in serving God.
questions.p: For Horeb, God no show for fire or wind, na small soft voice im take talk to Elijah. E con tell am say seven thousand pipo still dey wey never bow down for Baal, so Elijah no dey alone.

questions.q: Before he was taken up to heaven, Elijah asked Elisha what he wanted, and Elisha made a specific request. What did Elisha ask for from Elijah?
o: Half of Elijah's wealth and servants
Elijah's mantle as a keepsake only
Permission to succeed him immediately as king
A double portion of Elijah's spirit
questions.e: Elisha asked that a double portion of Elijah's spirit be upon him before his master was taken away. Elijah told him this was a hard request but granted it since Elisha saw him as he was taken up in the whirlwind.
questions.p: Elisha ask Elijah make im give am double portion of im spirit before dem carry am go. Elijah tell am say na hard thing, but if Elisha see am as dem dey carry am go, e go get am.

questions.q: Naaman initially became angry and almost turned away in disappointment when he received Elisha's instructions for his healing. What mainly caused his anger?
o: Elisha demanded a large sum of money before healing him
Elisha sent him to a foreign prophet instead of helping him directly
Elisha refused to see him in person and the instructions seemed too simple
Elisha asked him to first renounce his position as an army commander
questions.e: Naaman expected Elisha to come out, call on God, and wave his hand over the spot, so he was offended that the prophet did not even meet him and simply gave a simple instruction through a messenger. His servants later persuaded him to obey despite his pride.
questions.p: Naaman anger catch am because Elisha no even come out greet am personally, and the instruction wey Elisha give am through messenger look too simple. Na later im servants beg am make im obey the prophet.

questions.q: When Elisha's servant Gehazi deceitfully pursued Naaman to collect silver and garments after Elisha had refused any payment, what consequence did Elisha pronounce on him for this act of greed and lying?
o: Gehazi was struck with leprosy that would cling to him and his descendants
Gehazi was banished from Israel forever
Gehazi lost his position as Elisha's servant but suffered no illness
Gehazi was made to return double the goods he had collected
questions.e: Because Gehazi lied to Naaman and secretly took the gifts Elisha had refused, Elisha declared that Naaman's leprosy would cling to Gehazi and his descendants forever. Gehazi left the prophet's presence as a leper, white as snow.
questions.p: Because Gehazi follow Naaman go collect gift through lie-lie, Elisha curse am say Naaman leprosy go stick to am and im children forever. Gehazi waka leave the place white like snow with leprosy.

questions.q: During the siege of Samaria by the Syrians, Elisha prophesied that there would be abundant food in the city within a short time despite severe famine. What eventually caused this prophecy to be fulfilled?
o: Elisha personally multiplied the little food remaining in the city
The king of Israel surrendered the city peacefully to Syria
God caused the Syrian army to hear a noise of a great army and flee, leaving their supplies behind
Naaman sent food supplies from Syria as a gift to Elisha
questions.e: The Lord made the Syrian camp hear the sound of chariots and a great army, causing them to flee in panic and abandon their camp with all its provisions. Lepers outside the city discovered this and the news brought relief to starving Samaria, fulfilling Elisha's word.
questions.p: God make the Syrian army hear sound like say plenty soldiers dey come, so dem run leave all dia food and properties. Na so hunger finish for Samaria as Elisha talk am.

questions.q: Elijah's confrontation with Ahab over Naboth's vineyard shows a key role of the prophet in ancient Israel. Which of these best describes this role as demonstrated in that encounter?

The prophet served as a moral conscience who confronted rulers over injustice and sin
The prophet's duty was limited to predicting future events without addressing present conduct
The prophet acted mainly as a political adviser who helped kings expand their territory
questions.e: When Ahab seized Naboth's vineyard after Jezebel's wicked plot, Elijah boldly confronted the king, pronounced judgment, and held him accountable for the injustice. This shows that true prophets acted as God's voice against the sins of rulers, not merely as fortune-tellers.
questions.p: When Ahab collect Naboth vineyard through wicked way, Elijah go face am straight to tell am im sin. Dis show say true prophets dey speak against injustice and wickedness of kings.

questions.q: Why did Naaman request two mule-loads of earth to carry back to Syria after his healing was confirmed through his servants' persuasion to obey Elisha's instruction?

He needed the soil for medicinal purposes to prevent his disease from returning
He planned to give the earth to King Jehoram as tribute
He wanted to build an altar of Israelite soil to offer sacrifices only to the Lord
questions.e: After recognising that the God of Israel was the only true God, Naaman asked for soil from Israel so he could build an altar and offer sacrifices to the Lord alone, even back in Syria. This showed his genuine conversion and commitment to worship only the God who healed him.

He delayed the Passover until the temple was fully rebuilt

questions.q: A student compares the reforms of Asa and Jehoshaphat and notes that both kings shared one major weakness in their relationship with Israel or its rulers. What was this common weakness?

Both entered into alliances that displeased the Lord

Both refused to appoint judges in the land

That they should judge according to the customs of surrounding nations
That they judged only civil cases, not religious ones
That they judged not for man but for the Lord, who was with them in giving judgement

The high place built by Solomon for Chemosh

o: True reform must always begin with foreign military support
National leaders can please God by tolerating all forms of worship equally
Genuine leadership includes the duty to remove idolatry and restore proper worship of God
Religious reform is only valid when carried out by priests, not kings
questions.e: Despite their different methods and varying degrees of success, all four kings acted to remove idolatry and restore true worship of God among their people. This shows that godly leadership carries responsibility for the spiritual state of the nation.
questions.p: All di four kings try to commot idolatry and bring back true worship of God for dia land. Dis one show say good leader must care about di spiritual life of di nation.

questions.q: In Amos 4:1, the prophet addresses the wealthy women of Samaria by a scornful name because of their cruelty to the poor and their demand for luxury. What did he call them?

Daughters of Zion
Virgins of Israel
Kine of Bashan
questions.e: Amos called the pampered, oppressive women of Samaria 'kine (cows) of Bashan' because they crushed the poor and lived in luxury gotten through injustice. This picture shows how social oppression had reached even the homes of the wealthy.

o: They offered sacrifices while practising injustice and oppressing the poor
They refused to build a temple for proper worship
They stopped giving tithes to the priests
They worshipped foreign gods instead of Yahweh

questions.p: God reject Israel feast and song because dem dey oppress poor people while dem dey do religious show. Amos teach say true worship must follow justice and righteousness for everyday life.

o: That God condemns dishonest business practices done alongside empty religious observance
That trading on the Sabbath is the greatest sin in Israel
That keeping the Sabbath automatically guarantees God's blessing
That poverty is a sign of God's curse on dishonest traders
questions.e: Amos condemned merchants who could not wait for the Sabbath to end so they could cheat with false scales and overpriced goods. This shows that outward religious observance without honesty and justice is worthless to God.
questions.p: Amos condemn business people wey dey use false scale to cheat customers while dem dey keep Sabbath religiously. Dis show say physical religious observance without honesty na waste of time for God eye.

questions.q: In Amos's prophecy, God declares that He chose Israel alone out of all the families of the earth, yet He would still punish them. What reason does Amos give for this coming punishment?
o: Because Israel's population had become too small
Because of all their iniquities, including injustice against the poor
Because Israel had stopped paying taxes to the king
Because Israel refused to build more altars for sacrifice
questions.e: In Amos 3:2, God says He knew Israel above all nations, so He would punish them for their iniquities, especially their oppression of the poor and perversion of justice. Being chosen carried greater responsibility, not immunity from judgement.
questions.p: For Amos 3:2, God explain say because He choose Israel above all nations, He go punish dem for dia wickedness and oppression. To be God chosen people mean say person carry higher responsibility, no be say person get immunity from judgement.

questions.q: Hosea compares Israel's loyalty to God as being as fleeting and unreliable as two things mentioned in Hosea 6:4. What are these two things?
o: A dying lamp and a dry well
A broken pot and a torn garment
A fading flower and a withered tree
A morning cloud and the early dew that vanishes
questions.e: Hosea 6:4 says Israel's goodness and love for God were like a morning cloud and the early dew, both of which disappear quickly. This shows how temporary and shallow Israel's devotion to God had become.
questions.p: Hosea 6:4 talk say Israel love and goodness be like morning cloud and early dew wey dey vanish quick quick. Dis picture show how shallow and temporary dia devotion to God be.

questions.q: Both Amos and Hosea taught that true religion involves more than ritual sacrifices. Which statement best summarises this shared central message of the two prophets?
o: God only accepts worship performed in Jerusalem
Sacrifices are useless and should be completely abolished from worship
Genuine worship of God must be shown through justice, mercy and faithful living, not mere rituals
Only prophets can truly worship God acceptably
questions.e: Amos and Hosea both insisted that acceptable worship must be backed by justice, mercy, and loyalty to God's covenant, not empty rituals. Sacrifices without righteous living were condemned by both prophets.
questions.p: Both Amos and Hosea preach say God prefer justice, mercy and faithful living pass ordinary ritual sacrifices. Sacrifice wey no get righteous lifestyle get as e be for God.

questions.q: In Hosea 4:6, God laments that His people are destroyed for lack of a particular thing, which also led the prophet to warn that the priests who should have taught it would be rejected. What is this missing thing?
o: Rainfall
Soldiers
Knowledge
Silver
questions.e: Hosea 4:6 states that God's people were destroyed for lack of knowledge, meaning knowledge of God's law and ways which the priests failed to teach them. Because the priests rejected this knowledge, God also rejected them from serving as priests.
questions.p: Hosea 4:6 make us understand say God people destroy because dem lack knowledge of God law. Because di priests fail to teach di people, God talk say He go reject dem too.

questions.q: Amos warned that a certain disaster, often called 'the Day of the Lord', which Israel wrongly expected to bring them light and victory, would instead bring them what?
o: A new covenant with more priests
Freedom from the king of Assyria
Great wealth and abundant harvest
Darkness and judgement instead of light and relief
questions.e: In Amos 5:18-20, the prophet corrects Israel's false hope that the Day of the Lord would favour them; instead he says it will be darkness and not light, a day of inescapable judgement. This was because of their persistent injustice and false sense of security.
questions.p: Amos warn Israel say di Day of the Lord no go bring light and victory as dem dey expect, but na darkness and judgement. Dis na because of dia wicked lifestyle and false sense of security.

questions.q: In Isaiah's temple vision, the prophet described seeing the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up, with His train filling the temple. What did this scene reveal to Isaiah about God's nature?
o: God's loneliness in heaven
God's majesty and holiness
God's weakness before idols
God's anger towards Israel
questions.e: The vision of God on a high throne with His train filling the temple emphasised His supreme majesty and holiness. This set the tone for Isaiah's reaction of unworthiness.
questions.p: Dat vision wey Isaiah see show say God get too much power and e holy well-well. Na dat one make Isaiah come realize say e no fit stand before God because e no pure.

questions.q: Immediately after Isaiah's guilt was taken away and his sin purged by the burning coal, what was his response to God's question about who would go for Him?
o: He volunteered himself willingly
He asked God to send someone else
He kept silent out of fear
He requested more time to decide
questions.e: Once cleansed, Isaiah boldly answered, 'Here am I; send me.' This showed that true cleansing from sin leads to willing service for God.
questions.p: As soon as God clean Isaiah sin, e no waste time again. E tell God say make e send am, because e don ready to work for God.

questions.q: Jeremiah prophesied that under the new covenant, God would deal with sin in a way that was different from the old covenant arrangement. What was this new feature concerning forgiveness?
o: Sacrifices would increase to cover sin
Sin would be remembered forever as a warning
Sin would be punished immediately without mercy
Sin would be forgiven and remembered no more
questions.e: In Jeremiah 31:34, God promised to forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more. This marked a shift from constant animal sacrifices to complete divine forgiveness.
questions.p: Jeremiah talk say for di new covenant, God go forgive sin and e no go remember am again. Dis one different from di old time wey dem dey use animal sacrifice every time.

questions.q: A Sunday school teacher in Enugu explains that under the new covenant in Jeremiah 31, people would no longer need one person to teach another to know God. What reason did Jeremiah give for this change?
o: All would personally know God themselves
Teachers would become too expensive to pay
Priests would no longer be available
Scrolls of the law would be destroyed
questions.e: Jeremiah said all, from the least to the greatest, would know God directly because His law would be written in their hearts. This removed the need for external teaching about knowing the Lord.
questions.p: Jeremiah explain say for di new covenant, everybody go know God by demselves. God go write im law for dia heart, so dem no go need person teach dem again.

questions.q: Isaiah's call narrative shows a clear pattern: vision of God, confession of sin, cleansing, and then commission to service. What lesson does this pattern teach about genuine service to God?
o: Visions are unnecessary for true service
Service must come before any confession of sin
Holiness and purification should precede service
Only priests can experience such a call
questions.e: The order in Isaiah chapter 6 shows that an encounter with God's holiness exposes sin, which must be cleansed before one can be fit for divine service. This teaches that holiness is a necessary preparation for ministry.
questions.p: Isaiah story show say before you fit serve God, you must first see im holiness and make e clean your sin. Holiness na di first step for any person wey wan serve God.

questions.q: Comparing Isaiah's message of judgment with Jeremiah's new covenant promise, what common purpose did both prophecies ultimately serve for Israel?
o: To replace the temple with new buildings
To lead the nation towards repentance and renewed relationship with God
To condemn Israel without any hope of restoration
To encourage Israel to form alliances with foreign nations
questions.e: Though Isaiah's call included warnings of judgment and Jeremiah's new covenant offered hope, both ultimately aimed at turning Israel back to a right relationship with God. Judgment and promise worked together for Israel's spiritual restoration.
questions.p: Even though Isaiah talk about judgment and Jeremiah talk about new covenant, both of dem get one aim. Dem want make Israel repent and come back to God.

questions.q: After receiving his call, Isaiah was told that the people would hear but not understand, and see but not perceive. What did this aspect of his commission reveal about the nature of his prophetic task?
o: He was commanded to avoid speaking to the leaders
His message would be easily accepted by all
His task was limited only to foreigners
His ministry would involve preaching to a spiritually unresponsive people
questions.e: God warned Isaiah that the people's hearts were hardened, so they would hear without understanding. This meant his prophetic task would be difficult, preaching to a nation resistant to repentance.
questions.p: God tell Isaiah say di people heart don hard, so dem go hear but dem no go understand. Dis show say Isaiah work no go easy because di people no go wan listen.

questions.q: In Jeremiah chapter 31, God declared that the new covenant would not be like the one broken by the fathers whom He brought out of a certain land. Which event was this a reference to?
o: The building of Solomon's temple
The deliverance from slavery in Egypt
The crossing of the River Jordan into Canaan
The return from Babylonian exile
questions.e: Jeremiah 31:32 refers to the covenant made when God led the Israelites out of Egypt, which they later broke. The new covenant was presented as superior and unbreakable in comparison.
questions.p: Jeremiah 31:32 dey talk about di time wey God bring Israel comot from Egypt. Dat covenant wey dem make for dat time, di people break am, so God promise new one.

questions.q: In the vision recorded in Isaiah chapter 6, what did the seraphim use their wings for, according to the description of the heavenly beings around God's throne?
o: Two to shield the ark and four to fan incense before the altar
All six wings were used only for flying around the throne
Two to cover their faces, two to cover their feet, and two to fly
Four to cover their eyes and two to carry burning coals
questions.e: Isaiah 6 describes each seraph as having six wings: two covered the face, two covered the feet, and two were used for flying. This shows reverence before God's holiness.
questions.p: For Isaiah chapter 6, God angels wey dem dey call seraphim get six wings each. Dem dey use two cover dia face, two cover dia leg, and di other two naim dem dey use fly.

questions.q: When the posts of the temple door shook and the house was filled with smoke during Isaiah's vision, what was Isaiah's immediate reaction?
o: He cried out in fear, declaring himself a man of unclean lips among an unclean people
He asked God to send someone else immediately
He fell silent and worshipped without speaking
He rejoiced that God had answered his prayers
questions.e: Seeing the overwhelming holiness of God, Isaiah was struck with fear of his own sinfulness and that of his people, crying 'Woe is me! for I am undone'. This confession came before his cleansing and call.
questions.p: When Isaiah see how God holy sotay everywhere shake, e fear say e unclean. Naim e come shout say wahala don enter am because e be sinner man.

questions.q: A pastor teaching on Jeremiah's call narrative tells his congregation that before Jeremiah was formed in the womb, God had already appointed him for a special task. What was that task?
o: A king to rule over Judah
A prophet unto the nations
A priest to serve in the temple at Jerusalem
A scribe to copy the law of Moses
questions.e: In Jeremiah 1:5, God tells Jeremiah that before he was formed in the womb, he was known and ordained as a prophet unto the nations. This shows God's sovereign plan for Jeremiah's life.
questions.p: God tell Jeremiah before dem even born am for belle, say e don select am already. E make am prophet to carry message give all di nations.

questions.q: When Jeremiah protested his call by saying he was only a child and could not speak, how did God respond to strengthen him for the task ahead?
o: God sent an angel to anoint him with oil
God instructed him to wait until he was older
God gave him a scroll to swallow for wisdom
God told him not to be afraid and promised to be with him to deliver him
questions.e: In Jeremiah 1:7-8, God told Jeremiah not to say he was a child, but to go wherever he was sent and speak whatever he was commanded, assuring him of divine presence and deliverance. This encouragement addressed Jeremiah's fear of inadequacy.
questions.p: When Jeremiah yarn say e too small pikin wey no sabi talk, God tell am make e no fear. God promise say e go follow am go everywhere and rescue am.

questions.q: In Jeremiah's call, God touched the prophet's mouth and declared that he had put his words there. What two-fold purpose did God give for this appointment over nations and kingdoms?
o: To write laws and interpret dreams
To anoint kings and crown princes
To build and to plant, as well as to root out and to pull down
To collect tribute and enforce taxes
questions.e: Jeremiah 1:9-10 shows that God's hand touched Jeremiah's mouth and set him over nations to root out, pull down, destroy, throw down, build and plant. This dual mission of judgment and restoration defined his prophetic ministry.
questions.p: God touch Jeremiah mouth put word inside, con give am work over nations. E say make e root out, pull down, build, and also plant.

questions.q: A CRS teacher explains that Jeremiah saw a vision of an almond tree branch early in his call experience. What did God say this vision confirmed about his prophetic word?
o: That God was watching over his word to perform it
That God would delay judgment for many generations
That Jeremiah would plant trees as a sign of peace
That the almond tree symbolised Israel's wealth
questions.e: In Jeremiah 1:11-12, the vision of the almond rod (a play on the Hebrew word for 'watching') was interpreted by God as a sign that he was watching over his word to fulfil it. This assured Jeremiah that his prophecies would surely come to pass.
questions.p: God show Jeremiah almond tree branch to explain say E dey watch. Dis na to show say wetin God talk, E must surely make am happen.

questions.q: Under the new covenant described in Jeremiah 31, what did God promise concerning the relationship between himself and the people, beyond the forgiveness of sin?
o: He would rebuild the temple with gold and silver
He would appoint new kings to replace David's line
He would make them wealthy and give them many children
He would be their God and they would be his people
questions.e: Jeremiah 31:33 states that as part of the new covenant, God would write his law in their hearts and declares, 'I will be their God, and they shall be my people.' This shows a renewed, personal covenant relationship.
questions.p: For inside di new covenant for Jeremiah 31, God promise say E go be dia God and dem go be His people. E mean say relationship go tight well well.

questions.q: A student argues that Isaiah's call and Jeremiah's call both show prophets initially reluctant or afraid when confronted by God. Comparing the two accounts, what was the main difference in how each prophet expressed his hesitation?
o: Isaiah refused outright to go, while Jeremiah eagerly volunteered without hesitation
Isaiah demanded a sign before accepting, while Jeremiah demanded wealth
Isaiah feared his sinfulness before a holy God, while Jeremiah feared he was too young and inexperienced
Isaiah asked for a scroll to read, while Jeremiah asked for silver and gold
questions.e: Isaiah's hesitation came from seeing God's holiness and feeling unclean (Isaiah 6:5), while Jeremiah's hesitation was about his youth and inability to speak well (Jeremiah 1:6). Both were reassured by God before taking up their prophetic missions.
questions.p: Isaiah fear because e see say e unclean before God holiness, but Jeremiah talk say e too young. God come help both of dem overcome dia fear.

questions.q: Daniel and his three friends refused to eat the king's rich food and wine while in training at the Babylonian court. What did Daniel request instead, to prove that this diet was better for them?
o: Fruits and milk for a week
Vegetables and water for ten days
Meat and wine diluted with water
Bread and honey for a month
questions.e: Daniel asked the steward to test him and his friends with vegetables and water for ten days instead of the king's food. At the end, they looked healthier than those who ate the royal diet.
questions.p: Daniel tell di steward make e test dem wit vegetable and water for ten days instead of di king food. After di ten days, dem come look healthy pass all di oda pipo wey chop di king food.

questions.q: Daniel was thrown into a den of lions because he disobeyed a certain decree signed by King Darius. What exactly did this decree forbid?
o: Praying to any god or man except the king for thirty days
Eating food sacrificed to idols
Speaking against the king's officials in public
Bowing to any golden image set up by the king
questions.e: Jealous officials tricked King Darius into signing a decree that no one should pray to any god or man except the king for thirty days. Daniel continued praying to God three times a day and was thus cast into the lions' den.
questions.p: Some jealous pipo trick King Darius make e sign law say nobody suppose pray to any god or man except di king for thirty days. Daniel no gree, e continue to pray to God three times every day, na why dem throw am inside lion den.

questions.q: When Ezra returned to Jerusalem from Babylon, he discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had committed a particular sin that greatly troubled him. What was this sin?
o: They had stopped offering sacrifices in the temple
They had intermarried with foreign idol-worshipping peoples
They had rebuilt the wall without royal permission
They had refused to pay their tithes
questions.e: Ezra was told that the people, priests and Levites had intermarried with foreign nations and adopted their detestable practices. This grieved Ezra deeply, and he tore his garment and prayed in repentance on behalf of the nation.
questions.p: Ezra come hear say di Israelites, even di priests, don marry foreign women wey dey worship idol. Dis one pain Ezra well-well, e come tear im cloth and pray make God forgive dem.

questions.q: In Nehemiah's account, some wealthy Jews were exploiting their poorer kinsmen during the period of wall-building. What exactly were the rich nobles doing to the poor?
o: Charging interest and taking their fields, vineyards and children as pledges for loans
Selling them as slaves to the Samaritans
Forcing them to worship foreign gods
Refusing to let them join the rebuilding work
questions.e: The poor complained that they had to mortgage their fields and vineyards and even sell their children into servitude to pay taxes and buy grain, because the nobles charged them interest. Nehemiah rebuked the nobles and made them restore what they had taken.
questions.p: Di rich nobles dey charge di poor pipo interest and collect dia land and children as pledge. Nehemiah come vex for di nobles and tell dem say make dem return everything wey dem collect from di poor.

questions.q: Ezekiel performed several symbolic acts to warn Judah of coming judgment. What did it mean when God instructed him to lie on his left side for a fixed number of days and then on his right side for another fixed number?
o: He was mourning the death of his wife
He was demonstrating the length of the Babylonian captivity for all nations
He was showing how long the temple would take to rebuild
He was bearing the years of punishment for the sins of Israel and Judah
questions.e: God told Ezekiel to lie on his left side for 390 days to bear the sin of Israel and on his right side for 40 days to bear the sin of Judah, each day representing a year of their punishment. This dramatized the guilt and coming judgment on the two kingdoms.
questions.p: God tell Ezekiel make e lie for im left side for 390 days and right side for 40 days to show di punishment for Israel and Judah. Each day represent one year of di judgment wey go come meet dem.

questions.q: Nehemiah faced opposition from Sanballat and Tobiah, who tried several tactics to stop the wall-building project. Which of these was one of their strategies against Nehemiah personally?
o: They burned down the gates of Jerusalem
They poisoned the water supply of the workers
They invited him to a meeting on the plain of Ono to harm him
They bribed the king of Persia to recall him
questions.e: Sanballat and his allies repeatedly asked Nehemiah to meet them in one of the villages in the plain of Ono, intending to harm him, but Nehemiah refused, saying he was doing a great work and could not come down. This showed his discernment and determination.
questions.p: Sanballat and im pipo try trick Nehemiah make e come meet dem for Ono so dem go fit harm am. But Nehemiah wise, e tell dem say e dey do big work and e no fit come down.

questions.q: King Nebuchadnezzar was once driven away from human society and made to live like an animal, eating grass in the field, because of his pride over his kingdom's greatness. What restored his sanity and kingdom afterward?
o: He released all the Israelite captives in Babylon
He built a new temple to the God of Israel
He lifted his eyes to heaven and acknowledged that the Most High rules over all kingdoms
He consulted his wise men for a new interpretation
questions.e: After seven periods of time, Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he praised and honoured God as the one who rules the kingdom of men. His reason and kingdom were then restored to him.
questions.p: After Nebuchadnezzar suffer like animal for seven years, e come look up to heaven and recognize say na God get power over everything. Na dat time im sense come back and God restore im kingdom give am.

questions.q: When Ezra read the Law of Moses before the returned exiles at Jerusalem, the people reacted strongly on hearing its demands. What did Nehemiah and the Levites tell the weeping people to do instead?
o: Go home and sell their possessions for the temple
Rejoice, eat and share portions, for the joy of the Lord was their strength
Fast and mourn for seven days
Immediately leave their foreign wives
questions.e: When the people wept after hearing the Law, Nehemiah told them not to mourn but to go and eat, drink and send portions to those who had nothing, for the joy of the Lord was their strength. This turned the occasion into one of celebration rather than sorrow.
questions.p: When di pipo dey cry after dem hear di Law, Nehemiah tell dem say make dem no cry again. E tell dem make dem chop, drink, and share food wit oda pipo because di joy of di Lord na dia strength.

questions.q: When Mary visited Elizabeth after the annunciation, what happened to the baby in Elizabeth's womb?
o: He cried out loudly
He turned away
He became still and silent
He leaped for joy
questions.e: Luke records that when Mary greeted Elizabeth, the baby (John) leaped in her womb for joy. This confirmed to Elizabeth that Mary carried the Lord.
questions.p: As Mary greet Elizabeth, the baby wey dey inside Elizabeth belle jump for joy. Dis one show Elizabeth say Mary carry the Lord.

questions.q: According to Luke's gospel, what did the angel tell the shepherds would be the sign by which they could identify the newborn Christ?
o: A babe wrapped in swaddling clothes lying in a manger
A star standing still over the house
A voice speaking from the clouds
A dove descending from heaven
questions.e: The angel told the shepherds they would find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in a manger. This simple sign led them to Bethlehem to see Jesus.
questions.p: The angel tell the shepherds say dem go see the baby wey dem wrap for cloth inside manger. Na dat sign dem use find Jesus for Bethlehem.

questions.q: After the angel's announcement, a multitude of the heavenly host appeared praising God. What was the content of their praise as recorded in Luke?
o: Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord
Hosanna to the Son of David
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, goodwill toward men
Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts
questions.e: Luke records the heavenly host praising God with the words 'Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, goodwill toward men'. This is the well-known angelic chorus at Christ's birth.
questions.p: The heavenly host praise God say make glory dey for God for highest, and peace dey for earth for people wey God like. Na dat song dem sing when Jesus born.

questions.q: Joseph initially planned to put Mary away privately on discovering she was pregnant before marriage. What changed his mind?
o: Mary's parents pleaded with him
Elizabeth sent him a message
The priests in the temple advised him
An angel appeared to him in a dream and explained the pregnancy
questions.e: Matthew records that an angel appeared to Joseph in a dream, telling him not to fear to take Mary as his wife because her child was of the Holy Spirit. This made Joseph change his mind and take her home.
questions.p: Angel appear for Joseph for dream come tell am say make e no fear to marry Mary. E explain say the pikin na from Holy Spirit, so Joseph come change im mind.

questions.q: In Luke's account, after Jesus' birth his parents presented him in the temple at Jerusalem in obedience to the law of Moses. What was the main purpose of this presentation?
o: To register him as a citizen
