To redeem him as the firstborn and offer the required sacrifice
To dedicate him permanently to temple service like Samuel
To have him circumcised for the first time
questions.e: The law required that every firstborn male be presented to the Lord and redeemed with a sacrifice, which Mary and Joseph fulfilled by offering a pair of turtledoves. This fulfilled the Mosaic requirement, not a dedication to lifelong temple service.
questions.p: The law of Moses talk say make dem present every firstborn male for God and pay sacrifice. Mary and Joseph carry Jesus go temple to do wetin the law talk.

questions.q: Luke records that Jesus, at age twelve, stayed behind in the temple while his parents left Jerusalem. What was Jesus doing when his parents found him three days later?
o: Sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions
Sleeping in the temple courtyard
Praying alone in a corner of the temple
Selling merchandise in the temple court
questions.e: When his parents found Jesus, he was sitting among the teachers in the temple, listening to them and asking questions, and all who heard him were astonished at his understanding. This showed his early spiritual wisdom.
questions.p: When im parents find Jesus for temple, e dey sit down with the teachers. E dey listen to dem and dey ask dem question, and everybody surprise for im wisdom.

questions.q: John the Baptist's ministry in the wilderness of Judea fulfilled a prophecy about a voice crying in the wilderness. What was the central message of his preaching?
o: The coming destruction of Jerusalem
Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand
The restoration of King David's throne
The need to rebuild the temple
questions.e: John the Baptist's preaching centred on the call 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand', preparing people for the coming Messiah. This fulfilled Isaiah's prophecy of a voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the way of the Lord.
questions.p: John the Baptist message na say make people repent because the kingdom of heaven don near. E dey prepare the way for the Messiah as Isaiah talk.

questions.q: When John the Baptist baptised Jesus in the River Jordan, what two things immediately followed, confirming Jesus' identity?
o: Fire fell from heaven and consumed the riverbank
A rainbow appeared and angels sang over the water
An earthquake shook Jerusalem and the temple veil tore
The heavens opened with the Spirit descending like a dove and a voice declaring him God's beloved Son
questions.e: At Jesus' baptism, the heavens opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove upon him, and a voice from heaven declared, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased'. This event publicly confirmed Jesus' divine sonship at the start of his ministry.
questions.p: When Jesus baptize, heaven open and the Spirit come down like dove. One voice from heaven come talk say Jesus na im beloved Son wey e like.

questions.q: When John the Baptist hesitated to baptize Jesus, saying he needed to be baptized by Him instead, what reason did Jesus give for insisting on being baptized?
o: To receive forgiveness of His sins
To prove He was greater than John
To fulfil all righteousness
To show His humility before the crowd
questions.e: Jesus told John to allow it, 'for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness' (Matthew 3:15). This shows Jesus submitting to God's plan, not because He needed forgiveness.
questions.p: Jesus tell John make e allow am, 'cause na so dem suppose do everything wey dey righteous according to Matthew 3:15. Dis show say Jesus dey obey God plan, no be say e need forgiveness.

questions.q: During the second temptation, the devil took Jesus to the pinnacle of the temple and urged Him to jump down, quoting Scripture to support the suggestion. What did Jesus use to resist this temptation?
o: A counter-quotation from Scripture
A demand that the devil show his true form
A rebuke addressed directly to Satan by name
A call to His disciples for help
questions.e: Jesus replied, 'It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God' (Matthew 4:7). He answered each temptation by quoting Scripture correctly.
questions.p: Jesus answer am say, 'Dem write am again say, You no must tempt your Lord God' (Matthew 4:7). E use correct Scripture take answer every temptation wey come e way.

questions.q: In the third temptation, the devil offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and their glory on one condition. What was that condition?
o: That Jesus would fast for another forty days
That Jesus would fall down and worship him
That Jesus would deny being the Son of God
That Jesus would build him a temple
questions.e: The devil said, 'All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me' (Matthew 4:9). Jesus rejected this and commanded Satan to leave.
questions.p: The devil tell am say, 'I go give you all dis things if you go down and worship me' (Matthew 4:9). Jesus yab am comot and tell Satan make e waka.

questions.q: After Jesus overcame all three temptations in the wilderness, what happened to Him immediately afterward, according to the gospel account?
o: Angels came and ministered unto Him
John the Baptist came to congratulate Him
He was taken straight to Galilee by the Spirit
He fell asleep from exhaustion
questions.e: After the devil left Him, 'angels came and ministered unto him' (Matthew 4:11). This shows God's care for Jesus after His victory over temptation.
questions.p: After the devil waka leave am, 'angels come and help am' (Matthew 4:11). Dis one show how God dey look after Jesus after e win temptation.

questions.q: When Jesus called Matthew (Levi) to follow Him, Matthew was engaged in an occupation that was generally despised by his fellow Jews. What was this occupation?
o: Serving as a soldier for Herod
Fishing on the Sea of Galilee
Herding sheep in the countryside
Collecting taxes at a tax booth
questions.e: Matthew was sitting at the tax collector's booth when Jesus called him, and he immediately left it to follow Him (Matthew 9:9). Tax collectors were despised by Jews for working with Roman authorities.
questions.p: Matthew dey sit down for tax collector office when Jesus call am, and e quick follow am (Matthew 9:9). Jews no like tax collectors because dem dey work with Roman people.

questions.q: A Sunday School teacher in Enugu explains that Jesus did not choose His twelve disciples randomly but took a special step beforehand. What did Jesus do before selecting the twelve disciples, according to Luke's gospel?
o: He tested each candidate with a riddle
He consulted the chief priests for advice
He spent a whole night in prayer to God
He asked John the Baptist to choose for Him
questions.e: Luke 6:12 records that Jesus 'went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God' before choosing the twelve. This shows the importance of prayer in making major decisions.
questions.p: Luke 6:12 talk say Jesus 'go enter mountain to pray, and spend the whole night dey pray to God' before e pick the twelve. Dis show say prayer very important when person wan make big decision.

questions.q: Simon Peter and Andrew, together with James and John, were fellow fishermen before their call. What does this shared background mainly suggest about the kind of men Jesus chose as His first disciples?
o: They were already famous teachers of the law
They were ordinary working men, not religious scholars
They were priests trained in the temple
They were wealthy landowners with much influence
questions.e: Jesus called ordinary fishermen, not trained religious leaders, showing that God can use humble, everyday people for great purposes. This reflects a key lesson from the call narratives in the gospels.
questions.p: Jesus call ordinary fishermen, no be people wey dem train as religious leaders, to show say God fit use anybody for big work. E teach us say ordinary people matter for God eye.

questions.q: In the first temptation in the wilderness, the devil challenged Jesus to turn stones into bread. With what scripture did Jesus reply to the devil?
o: Get thee behind me, Satan
Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God
Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve
questions.e: Jesus quoted Deuteronomy to show that true life depends on obedience to God's word, not bread alone. This was His answer to the first temptation concerning hunger.
questions.p: Jesus use Deuteronomy tell devil say man no dey live by bread alone. E show say obedience to God word pass food for body.

questions.q: After calling Simon Peter, Andrew, James and John, Jesus went further into Galilee and called a tax collector sitting at the tax office. Where was this tax collector sitting when Jesus called him?
o: By the well of Samaria
At the city gate
At the entrance of the synagogue
At the receipt of custom
questions.e: Matthew (Levi) was sitting at the receipt of custom, the place where taxes were collected, when Jesus called him to follow Him. He immediately left his work to become a disciple.
questions.p: Matthew dey sit down for receipt of custom when Jesus call am. E leave all im work for tax office follow Jesus sharp sharp.

questions.q: A Sunday School teacher explains that when Jesus called His first four disciples by the Sea of Galilee, they responded in a particular manner that teaches Christians about discipleship today. Based on the Gospel account, how did Simon Peter, Andrew, James and John respond to the call?
o: They forsook their nets and family business and followed Him at once
They requested three days to consult their families first
They asked Jesus to first pay off their fishing debts
They followed Him only after He performed a miracle for them
questions.e: The Gospels record that the four fishermen left their nets and boats immediately to follow Jesus without delay or excuse. This prompt obedience is held up as a model of true discipleship.
questions.p: Dem four fishermen leave their net and work immediately follow Jesus. No be small time dem waste, dem just follow am straight.

questions.q: During the second temptation on the pinnacle of the temple, the devil quoted scripture to persuade Jesus to throw Himself down, claiming angels would bear Him up. How did Jesus respond to this misuse of scripture?
o: He said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
He remained silent and walked away
He said, Get thee hence, Satan
He said, Man shall not live by bread alone
questions.e: Jesus corrected the devil's twisting of scripture by quoting that one must not put the Lord God to the test. This shows Jesus countering every temptation with correct understanding of scripture.
questions.p: Jesus tell devil say make e no tempt God. E use correct scripture stop devil from misusing God word.

questions.q: At the pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, Jesus healed a man who had been afflicted for thirty-eight years. What hindered this man from being healed before Jesus met him?
o: He did not believe the pool had any healing power
The priests refused to let him enter the pool area
He had no one to help him into the pool when the water was troubled
He was too blind to find his way to the pool
questions.e: The man explained to Jesus that he had no one to put him into the pool when the water was stirred, and others always stepped in before him. Jesus healed him instantly by His word.
questions.p: Di man tell Jesus say nobody dey to help am enter inside di water when e move. Na so Jesus take im word heal am sharp-sharp.

questions.q: Jesus cast out a legion of demons from a man living among the tombs in the country of the Gadarenes. Into what animals did the demons beg to be allowed to enter?
o: A flock of sheep
A group of wild donkeys
A herd of cattle
A herd of swine
questions.e: The demons pleaded with Jesus to let them enter a herd of swine feeding nearby. After entering the pigs, the whole herd rushed down a steep place into the lake and drowned.
questions.p: Dem demons beg Jesus make e allow dem enter di pigs wey dey feed nearby. As dem enter, all di pigs run enter inside water come die.

questions.q: When Jesus healed a man with a withered hand in the synagogue, the Pharisees watched Him closely hoping to accuse Him. What was the main reason for their anger?
o: The man was a known sinner
The healing happened on the Sabbath day
Jesus healed without touching the man
Jesus demanded payment for the healing
questions.e: The Pharisees considered healing to be work, which they believed was unlawful on the Sabbath. Jesus rebuked their attitude by asking whether it was lawful to do good or harm on the Sabbath.
questions.p: Di Pharisees believe say healing na work, so dem no want make Jesus do am for Sabbath day. Jesus come tell dem say e good to do better thing for Sabbath.

questions.q: Jesus healed ten men suffering from leprosy as He travelled between Samaria and Galilee. What lesson does this miracle mainly teach about human conduct?
o: The need for gratitude after receiving a blessing
The danger of associating with foreigners
The necessity of sacrifice at the temple
The importance of fasting before seeking healing
questions.e: Out of the ten lepers healed, only one, a Samaritan, returned to thank Jesus. This miracle teaches the importance of showing gratitude for blessings received.
questions.p: Na only one person out of di ten lepers come back to thank Jesus. Dis miracle show say e dey very important to show gratitude when person do you better.

questions.q: While teaching by the lake, Jesus told Simon Peter to let down his nets after a night of catching nothing. What was the immediate result of Peter's obedience?
o: The boat sank because it was overloaded with water
Peter caught one large fish containing a coin
The nets caught such a large number of fish that they began to break
Peter caught nothing but later found fish on the shore
questions.e: When Peter obeyed and let down the nets, he caught so many fish that the nets began to break, and he had to call his partners to help. This miracle led Peter to leave everything and follow Jesus.
questions.p: As Peter obey Jesus and throw net, fish plenty reach where di net start to break. E come call im partners make dem come help am carry di fish.

questions.q: Jesus once healed the daughter of a Gentile woman from Tyre and Sidon who begged Him for help, even though He first spoke of being sent only to the lost sheep of Israel. What quality of this woman made Jesus grant her request?
o: Her wealth and social status
Her promise to convert to Judaism
Her membership of the synagogue
Her persistent faith despite initial refusal
questions.e: Although Jesus initially seemed to refuse because she was not of Israel, the woman humbly persisted in faith, comparing herself to a dog eating crumbs under the table. Jesus commended her great faith and healed her daughter from a distance.
questions.p: Even as Jesus talk say e come for Israel, di woman no give up. Jesus come praise her faith because she humble and persistent, so e heal her pikin.

questions.q: On a stormy night, Jesus walked on the surface of the Sea of Galilee toward His disciples' boat. What happened when Peter tried to walk on the water toward Jesus?
o: Peter drowned before Jesus could reach him
Peter began to sink after becoming afraid of the wind
Peter refused to step out of the boat at all
Peter walked confidently all the way to Jesus without any trouble
questions.e: Peter started walking on the water but became frightened by the strong wind and began to sink. Jesus caught him immediately and asked why he doubted.
questions.p: Peter start to walk on top water, but as e see say wind dey blow, e fear come start to sink. Jesus come hold am quick-quick and ask am why e doubt.

questions.q: Jesus healed a woman who had been bent over and unable to straighten herself for eighteen years, by laying His hands on her in the synagogue. What did Jesus call the cause of her condition when defending His action to the ruler of the synagogue?
o: A curse placed on her by her enemies
Punishment for her personal sins
A spirit of infirmity that had bound her
A disease common among her family
questions.e: Jesus described the woman as having been bound by a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years and said she, a daughter of Abraham, ought to be loosed on the Sabbath. This answered the synagogue ruler's objection that healing should not happen on that day.
questions.p: Jesus talk say na spirit of infirmity bind di woman for eighteen years. E come tell di synagogue ruler say e fit to heal her even for Sabbath day.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Mustard Seed, Jesus compared the kingdom of God to a mustard seed mainly to teach that the kingdom would
o: start small but grow into something very great
remain hidden and unknown forever
require costly planting to succeed
be destroyed before it could grow
questions.e: The mustard seed is the smallest of seeds but grows into a large tree. Jesus used this to show that the kingdom of God would start small and grow greatly.
questions.p: Na mustard seed dey small pass all seed, but e dey grow enter big tree. Jesus use am show say God kingdom go start small, but e go later big well well.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant, the king forgave his servant a very large debt, but that servant later refused to forgive a fellow servant who owed him a much smaller amount. What happened to the unforgiving servant when the king heard of this?
o: He was promoted to a higher position
He was handed over to the tormentors until he paid all he owed
He was given more wealth to manage
He was simply warned and released
questions.e: Because the servant refused to show the same mercy he had received, the angry king delivered him to the tormentors till he should pay all that was due. This teaches that believers must forgive others as God forgave them.
questions.p: Because the servant no gree show mercy to im fellow servant, the king vex and hand am over to tormentors until e pay everything. E dey teach us say make we dey forgive others as God don forgive us.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Good Shepherd, what quality of the shepherd showed his genuine love and ownership of the sheep, unlike the hired servant?
o: He sold the sheep for a good price
He counted the sheep every morning
He kept the sheep locked up permanently
He was willing to lay down his life for the sheep
questions.e: Jesus said the good shepherd gives his life for the sheep, while the hired servant flees when danger comes because the sheep are not his own. This illustrates Christ's sacrificial love for his people.
questions.p: Jesus talk say good shepherd dey give im life for im sheep, unlike person wey just dey work for money wey dey run when danger come. E show how Christ love im people reach to die for them.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Wise and Foolish Builders, the house built on the rock stood firm during the storm while the house on the sand fell. Jesus used this parable to teach that
o: sand is a poor material for all buildings
only skilled builders can construct strong houses
hearing and obeying his words brings a firm foundation for life
storms should always be avoided
questions.e: Jesus compared the man who hears and does his words to the wise builder on rock, and the one who hears but does not obey to the foolish builder on sand. The lesson is that obedience to Christ's teaching gives a solid foundation.
questions.p: Jesus compare person wey dey hear and do wetin e talk to wise builder wey build on rock. E mean say if you dey obey Christ word, your life go get strong foundation.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector who went up to the temple to pray, what made the tax collector's prayer acceptable to God rather than the Pharisee's?
o: He humbly confessed his sin and asked for mercy
He listed his good deeds before God
He prayed for a longer time than the Pharisee
He prayed loudly for all to hear
questions.e: The tax collector beat his breast and asked God for mercy on him, a sinner, while the Pharisee boasted of his own righteousness. Jesus said the humble tax collector went home justified rather than the proud Pharisee.
questions.p: Na the tax collector humba himself, beat im chest, and beg God for mercy as sinner. Jesus talk say na dat humba prayer God accept pass the proud Pharisee own.

questions.q: A farmer in the Parable of the Sower scattered seed, and Jesus explained that the seed sown among thorns represents hearers whose growth is choked by what?
o: Persecution and sudden trials
Lack of water during the dry season
Birds that ate up the seed immediately
The cares, riches and pleasures of this life
questions.e: Jesus explained that the thorny ground represents those who hear the word, but the cares, riches and pleasures of life choke it so that it brings no fruit to maturity. This differs from the seed eaten by birds or the seed on rocky ground that withers under trial.
questions.p: Jesus explain say the seed among thorns na people wey hear word, but wahala, money and enjoyment of this world go choke am make fruit no come out.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard, the landowner paid the labourers hired early in the morning the same wage as those hired late in the day. What did this parable mainly teach about God?
o: God rewards according to the number of hours worked
God is generous and gives grace according to his own will, not human merit
Landowners must always hire more workers than needed
Workers should always negotiate their wages firmly
questions.e: The landowner reminded the grumbling early workers that he had the right to be generous with his own money. This parable teaches that God's grace and reward are given freely according to his own purpose, not strictly by human effort.
questions.p: The owner of the farm talk say e get right to show mercy to anybody as e like. E dey teach us say God grace and reward na gift, no be by our own power or work.

questions.q: In the Parable of the Two Debtors which Jesus told to Simon the Pharisee, one debtor owed five hundred pence and the other fifty. Jesus used this story mainly to show that
o: rich debtors deserve more forgiveness than poor ones
forgiveness should only be granted to those who can repay fully
the woman who washed his feet loved much because she was forgiven much
Simon the Pharisee had committed a greater sin than the woman
questions.e: Jesus told Simon that the debtor forgiven the larger amount would love the creditor more, comparing this to the woman who showed great love by washing his feet because her many sins were forgiven. The lesson is that greater awareness of forgiveness produces greater love.
questions.p: Jesus use the story explain say anybody wey God forgive plenty sins go show plenty love. Na im make the woman wash im feet because God don forgive her plenty sin.

questions.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught His followers not to lay up treasures on earth but in heaven. What reason did He give for this instruction?
o: Earthly treasures attract moth, rust and thieves, but heavenly treasures are secure
Earthly riches are evil in themselves and must be avoided
Earthly wealth makes a man too busy to pray daily
Heavenly treasures can be seen by other people and bring honour
questions.e: Jesus said moth and rust corrupt and thieves break through to steal earthly treasure, but treasure in heaven cannot be destroyed or stolen. The lesson is to set one's heart on lasting, godly priorities.
questions.p: Na wetin Jesus tok be sey, moth and rust dey spoil earthly treasure, and thief dey come thief am, but heaven treasure dey secure. Di lesson na sey make we focus our mind for heavenly things wey no dey perish.

questions.q: Jesus warned His disciples in Matthew chapter 6 about practising their righteousness, such as giving alms, to be seen of men. What did He say would be the consequence of such practice?
o: God would multiply their wealth as a sign of approval
Their gift would be rejected by the needy who notice their pride
They would receive double blessing from God for their generosity
They have their reward already and will receive nothing from the Father
questions.e: Jesus taught that those who give alms publicly to be praised by men have already received their reward in full from men. True giving should be done secretly so that the Father who sees in secret will reward openly.
questions.p: Jesus explain sey anybody wey dey give alms for open place just to make people praise am don collect im reward for person hand finish. Make we dey do our good deeds for secret so dat God wey dey see for secret go reward us open.

questions.q: In His teaching on fasting, Jesus instructed that when His followers fast, they should anoint their head and wash their face. What was the main purpose of this instruction?
o: To prepare the body for a feast after the fast ends
To appear outwardly cheerful so that only God, not men, notices the fast
To impress religious leaders with proper fasting etiquette
To follow a tradition required before entering the temple
questions.e: Jesus told His disciples to appear normal and refreshed while fasting so that people would not notice, unlike the hypocrites who disfigured their faces to be seen fasting. This way, only the Father who sees in secret rewards them.
questions.p: Jesus tell im disciples make dem wash their face and rub oil when dem dey fast so dat people no go know sey dem dey fast. Na so only God wey dey see for secret go reward dem, instead make dem form holy for eye of man.

questions.q: Jesus said, "A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit." In the context of His warning against false prophets, what lesson is being taught?
o: Only trained religious leaders can correctly interpret scripture
Prophets must perform miracles to prove they are sent by God
True character and teaching are revealed by the quality of a person's actions and life
People should plant only fruitful trees in their farms for good harvest
questions.e: Jesus used the tree and fruit illustration to teach that genuine prophets are known by their actions and results, not merely their words or claims. A person's true nature is revealed through the consistent fruit of their life.
questions.p: Jesus use tree and fruit tok sey make we know true prophet by di kind life wey dem dey live and wetin dem dey do. Person true character dey show for di kind fruit wey im life dey produce.

questions.q: During the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught about the eye being the light of the body, saying that if the eye is single, the whole body shall be full of light. What is the central lesson of this teaching?
o: A person's focus and inner intention determine the moral direction of the whole life
Believers should avoid looking at worldly things completely
Physical eyesight determines a person's spiritual understanding
Good eyesight is a sign of God's blessing on a person
questions.e: Jesus used the eye as a symbol of one's inner focus or intention; a sound, single focus on God fills the whole life with light, while a divided or evil focus brings darkness. This links directly to His teaching on not serving two masters.
questions.p: Jesus use eye as symbol of our inner focus, meaning sey if your mind clear and focus for God, your whole life go dey full of light. Di way you take dey see things spiritually dey determine how your life go be.

questions.q: In Matthew chapter 7, Jesus warned His followers against judging others harshly, using the illustration of a mote and a beam. What does the beam in a person's own eye represent?
o: A physical object that blinds people from seeing clearly
The larger fault or sin in the critic's own life which he overlooks while condemning others
A small, forgivable mistake that everyone struggles with
The burden of responsibility given to religious leaders
questions.e: Jesus contrasted the small mote in another's eye with the large beam in the critic's own eye to show that people often magnify others' faults while ignoring their own greater faults. The lesson warns against hypocritical judgment.
questions.p: Di beam for person eye represent di big sin or fault wey di person get for im own life, but e dey busy dey judge small error for another person eye. Jesus use am warn us against hypocritical judgment.

questions.q: Jesus taught that true disciples are known not by merely saying "Lord, Lord" but by something else. According to this teaching in Matthew chapter 7, what truly qualifies a person to enter the kingdom of heaven?
o: Belonging to a recognised religious group or synagogue
Preaching publicly and prophesying to large crowds
Performing great miracles and casting out demons in Jesus' name
Doing the will of the Father which is in heaven
questions.e: Jesus warned that many would claim to have prophesied and done wonders in His name, yet He will reject them because they practised iniquity. True entrance into the kingdom depends on obedience to the Father's will, not impressive words or deeds alone.
questions.p: Jesus warn us sey no be everybody wey dey call 'Lord, Lord' or dey do miracle go enter kingdom of heaven, na only those wey dey do di will of God. Obedience to God na im matter pass.

questions.q: During the trial before the Sanhedrin, the chief priests brought false witnesses against Jesus, but their testimonies could not agree. What did the High Priest finally ask Jesus directly to force an answer?
o: Whether He had healed on the Sabbath
Whether He claimed to be a prophet like Moses
Whether He was the Christ, the Son of the Blessed
Whether He would destroy the temple in three days
questions.e: The High Priest asked Jesus plainly whether He was the Christ, the Son of the Blessed, and Jesus answered 'I am'. This answer was then used as the basis to declare Him guilty of blasphemy.
questions.p: High Priest ask Jesus straight if He be Christ, the Son of God. Jesus tell am say 'I am', and na dat word dem use call am blasphemy.

questions.q: When Pilate found no fault in Jesus, he sent Him to another ruler because Jesus was from Galilee. Who was this ruler?
o: Annas
Felix
Caiaphas
Herod Antipas
questions.e: Pilate learnt that Jesus belonged to Herod's jurisdiction and sent Him to Herod Antipas, who was in Jerusalem at that time. Herod questioned Jesus but Jesus refused to answer him.
questions.p: Pilate know say Jesus na Galilee man, so e send am go meet Herod Antipas wey dey Jerusalem dat time. Herod ask Jesus question but Jesus no answer am at all.

questions.q: As Jesus hung on the cross, He spoke certain words concerning those who crucified Him. What did He say about them?
o: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do
It is well with my soul
Vengeance belongs to the Lord
Father, let Your will be done on earth
questions.e: While dying on the cross, Jesus prayed for His killers, saying 'Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do'. This showed His spirit of forgiveness even in suffering.
questions.p: When dem dey crucify Jesus, e pray for dem say make God forgive dem because dem no know wetin dem dey do. Dis show say Jesus get big heart to forgive even when e dey suffer.

questions.q: On the cross, Jesus made a statement that showed His mission of redemption had been fully accomplished. Which of these was that statement?
o: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me
It is finished
Woman, behold thy son
I thirst
questions.e: Just before He died, Jesus declared 'It is finished', showing that the work of salvation He came to do was complete. This is one of the last sayings of Jesus on the cross.
questions.p: Before Jesus die, e shout say 'It is finished'. Dis mean say the work wey God send am come do for earth to save man don complete.

questions.q: On the evening of the resurrection day, two disciples travelling to a certain village met Jesus but did not recognise Him until He broke bread with them. Which village were they travelling to?
o: Capernaum
Emmaus
Bethphage
Bethany
questions.e: The two disciples were walking to Emmaus when the risen Jesus joined them on the road. They only recognised Him when He took bread, blessed and broke it at their meal.
questions.p: The two disciples dey go Emmaus when Jesus join dem for road. Dem no know say na Jesus until e break bread give dem.

questions.q: On the night of His resurrection, Jesus appeared to His disciples in a locked room and showed them His hands and side. Why did He show them these wounds?
o: To prove that He was truly the same Jesus who was crucified
To show them where the soldiers had pierced Him for the first time
To ask them to anoint His wounds with oil
To teach them how to treat the sick
questions.e: Jesus showed His hands and side so the disciples would be convinced He had truly risen in the same body that was crucified, not a ghost. This removed their fear and confirmed His resurrection.
questions.p: Jesus show dem e hand and e side so dem go know say na true true e rise from death. E want make dem believe say na the same body wey dem crucify, no be ghost.

questions.q: Before His ascension, Jesus gave His disciples a command concerning Jerusalem and the Holy Spirit. What exactly did He instruct them to do?
o: Choose a replacement for Judas before He left
Return immediately to Galilee and begin preaching
Tarry in Jerusalem until they received power from on high
Go into all Judea and build a temple
questions.e: Jesus told His disciples not to leave Jerusalem but to wait there until they were clothed with power from the Holy Spirit. This instruction prepared them for the coming of the Spirit at Pentecost.
questions.p: Jesus tell e disciples make dem no comot for Jerusalem. E tell dem say make dem wait there until Holy Spirit come give dem power.

questions.q: A careful reading of the resurrection and ascension accounts shows a definite order of events. Which sequence correctly arranges these events as they happened?
o: Appearance to Mary, ascension, empty tomb discovered, appearance to disciples
Ascension, empty tomb, appearance to Mary, appearance to disciples
Appearance to disciples, empty tomb, ascension, appearance to Mary
Empty tomb discovered, appearance to Mary, appearance to disciples, ascension
questions.e: The tomb was found empty first, then Jesus appeared to Mary Magdalene, afterwards He appeared to His disciples on several occasions, and finally He ascended into heaven. This is the correct historical order of the events in the gospel accounts.
questions.p: First, dem see say the tomb empty, then Jesus show e self to Mary Magdalene. After, e appear to the disciples before e finally go heaven.

questions.q: When Peter and John were brought before the Sanhedrin for healing the lame man, what did they boldly declare about the name by which the man was healed?
o: That the name must be kept secret from the Jewish council
That there is no other name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved
That the healing came through the merit of the apostles' own faith alone
That the name of Moses had power greater than any other
questions.e: Peter declared before the Sanhedrin that salvation is found in no other name but that of Jesus Christ. This was a bold confession of faith before hostile authorities.
questions.p: Peter tell the people for Sanhedrin say na only for Jesus name salvation dey. E talkam boldly sake of say e no fear the people wey holdam.

questions.q: In Acts chapter 5, what punishment befell Ananias and Sapphira after they lied to the Holy Spirit about the proceeds of their land?
o: They were both struck dead instantly
They were imprisoned by the apostles
They were expelled from the church by Peter
They were made to repay double the amount
questions.e: Ananias and Sapphira each fell down and died immediately after lying to the Holy Spirit concerning the sale of their property. Their sudden deaths brought great fear upon the whole church.
questions.p: Ananias and Sapphira fall down and die straight when dem tell lie about the money from their land. Their sudden death make fear catch everybody for church.

questions.q: Why did the Hellenist believers complain against the Hebrews in the early Jerusalem church, leading to the appointment of seven men including Stephen?
o: They wanted a separate place of worship
They were denied the right to preach in the temple
Their widows were neglected in the daily distribution of food
They were excluded from the apostles' teaching sessions
questions.e: The Grecian Jewish widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food, which caused murmuring. To resolve this, seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom were chosen to oversee the task.
questions.p: Wahala start because dem dey forget Hellenist widows for food sharing every day. To settle am, dem choose seven wise men wey get Holy Spirit.

questions.q: What was the main qualification required of the seven men chosen to serve tables in Acts chapter 6?
o: They had to be wealthy members who could fund the church
They had to be relatives of the twelve apostles
They had to be former priests converted to the faith
They had to be of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom
questions.e: The apostles instructed the believers to choose men of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom. Stephen was one of those selected for this responsibility.
questions.p: The apostles tell the people make dem choose men wey get better name, full of Holy Spirit and wisdom. Na so dem take pick Stephen and six other men.

questions.q: Before he was stoned, Stephen looked up to heaven and testified to seeing a vision. What did he say he saw?
o: The heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God
A great multitude of angels singing praises
A dove descending with an olive branch
An empty throne surrounded by bright light
questions.e: Stephen declared that he saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God. This enraged the council and led them to rush upon him and stone him.
questions.p: Before dem stone Stephen, e look up and talk say e see heaven open and Son of Man dey stand for God right hand. This one make the council vex well well.

questions.q: What prayer did Stephen offer for his killers just before he died from stoning?
o: Lord, let their children suffer for this act
Father, remember them not on the day of judgement
Lord, lay not this sin to their charge
Father, send fire upon them for their wickedness
questions.e: As he was dying, Stephen knelt and cried out asking the Lord not to hold the sin against his killers. This mirrored the spirit of forgiveness shown by Christ on the cross.
questions.p: As dem dey stone Stephen, e bend down and beg God make e no put the sin for their head. E show the same forgiveness wey Jesus show for cross.

questions.q: Which event in Acts chapter 12 shows that the early church depended on fervent prayer when a leader faced persecution from the state?
o: The apostles bribed the guards to free Peter
The church prayed earnestly and Peter was miraculously released from prison by an angel
The church fasted and Herod immediately repented
The believers hid Peter in a cave outside Jerusalem
questions.e: When Herod imprisoned Peter, the church prayed without ceasing, and an angel appeared to free him from his chains and lead him past the guards. This showed the power of united prayer during persecution.
questions.p: When Herod put Peter for prison, church con pray well well foram, and angel come removeam from chains. E show say prayer get power when wahala come.

questions.q: A new convert in Lagos argues that the early church's growth under persecution proves that suffering for one's faith can actually strengthen the spread of the gospel. Which incident from Acts best supports this reasoning?
o: The believers sought revenge against those who persecuted them
The church stopped growing until the persecution ended completely
The apostles abandoned the ministry to avoid further trouble
Believers scattered by persecution preached the word wherever they went, spreading the gospel beyond Jerusalem
questions.e: Although persecution scattered the believers from Jerusalem, they preached the gospel wherever they went, causing the church to spread further. This shows that suffering did not stop the mission but helped extend it.
questions.p: Even though wahala scatter the believers, dem still dey preach the word anywhere dem go. This one show say persecution even help gospel reach another place.

questions.q: Immediately after his sight was restored in Damascus, what did Saul do before he began to preach Christ in the synagogues?
o: He went into Arabia for three years
He was baptised and took food to regain strength
He fasted for forty days in the wilderness
He returned to Jerusalem to consult the apostles
questions.e: After Ananias prayed for him, Saul received his sight, was baptised, and ate food to strengthen himself before he began preaching. This happened in Damascus, not Jerusalem or Arabia at that point.
questions.p: After Ananias pray for Saul, e eyes open, e baptize, and chop food to get strength before e start to preach. Na for Damascus all dis one happen, no be Jerusalem or Arabia.

questions.q: When the believers in Jerusalem first heard that Saul wanted to join them, how did they react?
o: They were afraid of him because they doubted his conversion was real
They sent him immediately to preach to the Gentiles
They welcomed him joyfully as a fellow apostle
They asked him to prove himself by healing a sick man
questions.e: The disciples in Jerusalem were afraid of Saul and did not believe he was truly a disciple, until Barnabas brought him to the apostles and explained his conversion.
questions.p: The disciples for Jerusalem fear Saul well-well because dem no believe say e don truly change. Na Barnabas come carry am go meet the apostles to explain wetin happen.

questions.q: On Paul's first missionary journey, what happened to the sorcerer Elymas at Paphos when he tried to turn the Roman proconsul away from the faith?
o: He was driven out of the city by soldiers
He was stoned by the crowd
He was struck blind for a season
He repented and was baptised at once
questions.e: Paul rebuked Elymas the sorcerer for opposing the gospel, and he was struck blind for a time, which led the proconsul Sergius Paulus to believe.
questions.p: Paul rebuke the sorcerer Elymas because e dey block the gospel. God come make the man blind for some time, and dis one make the proconsul believe.

questions.q: At Lystra, how did the crowd react after Paul healed a man who had been lame from birth?
o: They demanded that the man be examined by the priests
They mocked Paul and Barnabas and chased them away
They stoned Paul immediately without listening to him
They tried to offer sacrifices to Paul and Barnabas, calling them gods
questions.e: After the healing at Lystra, the crowd thought Barnabas was Zeus and Paul was Hermes, and the priest of Zeus brought oxen to sacrifice to them, until Paul and Barnabas stopped them.
questions.p: After Paul heal the lame man for Lystra, the people think say Paul and Barnabas na gods. The priest of Zeus even wan bring cow come sacrifice for dem, but dem stop am.

questions.q: Which event caused the sharp disagreement between Paul and Barnabas that led them to separate before the second missionary journey?
o: A disagreement over taking John Mark along again
A conflict over preaching in the synagogue first
A dispute about who should lead the journey
A quarrel over whether to visit Jerusalem first
questions.e: Barnabas wanted to take John Mark, who had earlier deserted them in Pamphylia, but Paul refused, causing a sharp disagreement so that they parted ways, with Barnabas taking Mark to Cyprus and Paul choosing Silas.
questions.p: Barnabas want make dem carry John Mark go again, but Paul no gree because Mark bin leave dem before. The matter come hot reach say dem separate, Barnabas carry Mark go Cyprus, Paul carry Silas.

questions.q: During his second missionary journey, Paul had a vision of a man from which region begging him, 'Come over and help us', which led him to cross into Europe?
o: Cappadocia
Bithynia
Macedonia
Galatia
questions.e: At Troas, Paul saw a vision of a man of Macedonia pleading for help, and he understood this as God's call to preach the gospel in Macedonia, leading to the journey into Europe.
questions.p: When Paul dey Troas, e see vision of one man from Macedonia wey dey beg am say make e come help dem. Paul come know say na God call am to go preach for Macedonia.

questions.q: What was the main reason some believers from Judea insisted that Gentile converts must be circumcised, an issue that eventually led to the Council of Jerusalem?
o: They wanted Gentiles to pay temple tax before joining the church
They feared Gentile converts would corrupt Jewish customs in worship
They wanted to test the loyalty of Gentile believers to Paul
They believed circumcision was required for one to be saved according to the law of Moses
questions.e: Certain men from Judea taught that unless Gentile believers were circumcised according to the custom of Moses, they could not be saved, and this teaching caused the dispute that was settled at Jerusalem.
questions.p: Some people from Judea dey teach say if Gentile no circumcise like Moses law, dem no fit save. Dis teaching na im cause the big wahala wey dem go settle for Jerusalem.

questions.q: At the Council of Jerusalem, which apostle's account of God working signs and wonders among the Gentiles helped to convince the assembly alongside Peter's speech?
o: John the beloved disciple
Paul and Barnabas
Philip the evangelist
James, the brother of the Lord
questions.e: After Peter spoke, Paul and Barnabas gave testimony of the miracles and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them, and this testimony, along with James's judgement, helped settle the matter.
questions.p: After Peter talk, Paul and Barnabas come tell the people how God take do signs and wonders among the Gentiles. Dis testimony help the council reach decision.

questions.q: In Romans 4, Paul uses Abraham as an example to teach justification by faith. According to this chapter, Abraham's faith was credited to him as righteousness before he was circumcised, proving that he became the father of all who believe. What does this example primarily establish?
o: That Abraham earned righteousness through his good deeds
That circumcision is required before justification can occur
That only circumcised people can be justified
That righteousness comes by believing God, not by keeping ritual law
questions.e: Paul shows Abraham was declared righteous by faith before he was circumcised, proving justification is by faith and not by ritual observance like circumcision.
questions.p: Paul explain say God take Abraham righteous before e circumcision, dis show say na faith dey make person righteous, no be by ordinary ritual law.

questions.q: In 1 Corinthians 13:1-3, Paul says that even if he speaks with the tongues of men and angels, gives all his goods to feed the poor, and has faith to remove mountains, but has not love, he is nothing. What lesson does Paul teach through this statement?
o: Tongues are the greatest spiritual gift
Faith alone is sufficient without any other virtue
Spiritual gifts and sacrifice are worthless without love
Giving to the poor guarantees salvation
questions.e: Paul teaches that without love, even the most impressive gifts and sacrifices amount to nothing, showing love as the controlling virtue for all Christian service.
questions.p: Paul dey teach us say even if you get big-big spiritual gift or do sharp sacrifice, if love no dey inside your heart, you no be anything at all.

questions.q: According to Galatians 5:4, what does Paul warn happens to those who seek to be justified by the law?
o: They are severed from Christ and fallen from grace
They become stronger in their faith
They are given greater spiritual gifts
They receive a double portion of grace
questions.e: Paul warns that trying to be justified by law-keeping cuts a person off from Christ and grace, since grace and law-based self-justification cannot be mixed as the basis of salvation.
questions.p: Paul warn us say anybody wey wan use law save himself don cut off from Christ and grace, because grace and law-based self-justification no fit jam together.

questions.q: In Romans 6:14-15, Paul teaches that believers are not under law but under grace. He then asks a rhetorical question to correct a wrong conclusion some might draw from this teaching. What wrong conclusion is Paul correcting?
o: That believers should return to keeping the law strictly
That being under grace gives believers freedom to continue sinning
That grace removes the need for faith
That the law was never good in the first place
questions.e: Paul asks 'shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace?' to correct the false idea that grace is a license to sin, insisting believers must still live righteously.
questions.p: Paul ask question say make we continue to dey sin because we dey under grace? E do dis one to correct dis wrong mind-set, con tell us say we must still live well.

questions.q: According to 1 Corinthians 12:4-6, Paul describes spiritual gifts, ministries and workings among believers. What truth does he emphasise about the source of these different gifts?
o: Only apostles receive genuine spiritual gifts
Believers create their own gifts through effort
They come from different spirits competing with each other
They all come from the same God, Spirit and Lord
questions.e: Paul stresses that despite the diversity of gifts, ministries and activities, they all originate from the same Spirit, Lord and God, showing unity in diversity.
questions.p: Paul make am clear say even though the spiritual gift and work plenty, na just one Spirit, one Lord, and one God dey give all of them.

questions.q: In 1 Corinthians 13:11, Paul compares spiritual maturity to growing out of childish ways, saying that when he became a man he put away childish things. What point is Paul making by this comparison?
o: Children cannot receive the Holy Spirit
Maturity means abandoning all spiritual gifts
Love is a mark of spiritual maturity that surpasses partial gifts
Spiritual gifts are only for young believers
questions.e: Paul uses growing from childhood to adulthood to illustrate that present spiritual gifts are partial and will give way to the greater, lasting reality of love.
questions.p: Paul use how pesin take grow from pikin to adult explain say, love pass all dis spiritual gift wey go soon pass away.

questions.q: According to Romans 13:8-10, Paul teaches that love is the fulfilling of the law. Which of the following best explains how Paul supports this claim?
o: He argues that love only applies to fellow believers, not neighbours
He shows that commandments like 'do not steal' and 'do not kill' are summed up in loving one's neighbour
He says love replaces the need for the Ten Commandments entirely
He states that love makes obedience to any command unnecessary
questions.e: Paul lists commandments such as against adultery, murder and theft, then shows they are all summed up in the command to love one's neighbour, so genuine love fulfils the law's demands.
questions.p: Paul list commandment like make you no steal or kill, con show say all of them join together for the command to love your neighbour as yourself.

questions.q: In Ephesians 2:8-9, Paul explains that believers are saved by grace through faith, and this is not of themselves but is the gift of God. What does Paul specifically deny as the basis of this salvation?
o: That salvation is by works, so that no one may boast
That grace is freely given by God
That salvation can be received by anyone at all
That faith plays any role in salvation
questions.e: Paul clearly states salvation is not by works, so that no person can boast of earning it themselves; it is entirely God's gift received through faith.
questions.p: Paul yarn say salvation no come from our own work, so that nobody go carry chest dey yab say naim do am; na pure gift from God through faith.

questions.q: In Romans 12:3, Paul warns believers not to think of themselves more highly than they ought to think, but to think soberly. What virtue is Paul teaching here?
o: Diligence
Patience
Generosity
Humility
questions.e: Paul tells believers to have sober, modest self-assessment rather than pride. This is a direct call to humility among Christians using their different gifts.
questions.p: Paul dey tell Christians make dem no think say dem pass body, but make dem get correct sense of modesty. Na true humility im dey teach us so.

questions.q: In Galatians 6:2, Paul instructs believers to bear one another's burdens. According to the same verse, what law do they fulfil by doing this?
o: The law of the Spirit
The law of liberty
The law of Christ
The law of Moses
questions.e: Galatians 6:2 says bearing one another's burdens fulfils the law of Christ, which is the law of love. This teaches mutual care and humility within the Christian community.
questions.p: E clear say if we carry each other burden, na im be say we dey follow the law of Christ. Na love and care be the koko of that teaching.

questions.q: In 1 Peter 5:5-6, Peter urges younger believers to submit to elders, and all to clothe themselves with humility. He warns that God resists a particular group of people. Who are they?
o: The rich
The proud
The weak
The poor
questions.e: 1 Peter 5:5 states that God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble. Peter therefore calls believers to humble themselves under God's mighty hand.
questions.p: Bible tok am straight say God no like people wey get pride for body at all. Na why Peter advise everybody make dem humble theirself under God.

questions.q: In 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17, Paul describes the sequence of events at the Lord's return. According to this passage, what happens to the dead in Christ before the living believers are caught up to meet the Lord?
o: They rise first
They are purified
They remain asleep forever
They are judged first
questions.e: Paul teaches that the dead in Christ shall rise first, and then believers who are alive shall be caught up together with them to meet the Lord in the air. This order shows that death does not disadvantage believers who have died before Christ's return.
questions.p: Paul explain say the people wey don die for Christ go first wake up before the ones wey still dey alive. Dem go join together to meet Jesus for air.

questions.q: In 2 Thessalonians 3:10-12, Paul addresses believers who were idle and disorderly, refusing to work while expecting the Lord's return. What instruction does Paul give concerning such people?
o: They should be fed by the church daily
If any would not work, neither should he eat
They should be sent away from the city
They should be given double portions of food
questions.e: Paul rebukes idleness by stating that if anyone refuses to work, he should not eat. This teaches that expecting Christ's second coming does not excuse believers from responsible, diligent labour.
questions.p: Paul warn say person wey no gree work make im no chop food at all. E show say waiting for Jesus second coming no mean say make person lazy.

questions.q: In 2 Peter 3:8, Peter corrects wrong ideas about the delay of the Lord's coming by comparing a thousand years to what?
o: A generation
A single moment
One day
A lifetime
questions.e: Peter writes that with the Lord, one day is as a thousand years and a thousand years as one day. This teaches that God's timing differs from human timing, so believers should not mistake patience for delay.
questions.p: Peter make us understand say one day for God eyes be like thousand years. E show say God time no be human time at all.

questions.q: Consider these two statements about Hebrews chapter 13: (I) Believers are told to remember those in prison as if bound with them. (II) Believers are told to be content with such things as they have, for God will never leave them. Which of these statements correctly reflects teachings on Christian living in Hebrews 13?
o: Only statement I is correct
Only statement II is correct
Both statements are correct
Neither statement is correct
questions.e: Hebrews 13:3 instructs believers to remember prisoners as bound with them, and Hebrews 13:5 teaches contentment because God has promised never to leave nor forsake His people. Both teachings form part of the practical Christian living instructions in that chapter.
questions.p: Hebrews chapter 13 tell us say make we remember prisoners and also make we contented with wetin we get. Both instructions correct well well for Christian life.
